brethren. Esp. with the Midianites (Genesis 37:28 ), Midian being his half-brother, by Keturah (compare Judges 8:22 , Judges 8:24 ). Compare the fulfillment in Genesis 25:18 .

entries.title: GOD.
entries.content:
GOD. Hebrew. 'el . See App-4 .

said. Translate: "Do I see, here, even after the Vision? "i.e. "Do I live, after seeing God? "

looked = Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), implying living as well as looking Compare Genesis 32:30 . Judges 13:22 .

entries.title: Beer-lahai-roi
entries.content: Beer-lahai-roi = the well of living after seeing.

entries.title: Hagar bare.
entries.content: Hagar bare. Through infirmity of Sarah's faith. So the Law (parenthetically) "because of transgression" (Galatians 1:3 , Galatians 1:19 ). Levitical Law given, as Ishmael was, until Christ the antitype of Isaac should be born (Galatians 1:1-5 , Galatians 1:19 , Gal 1:31 ).

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

Almighty GOD = El Shaddai. First occ See App-4 . This title assures Abram that He Who had called him was almighty to supply all his need. Compare first occurance in N.T. (2 Corinthians 6:18 ), which assures us of the same supply.

walk = continue to walk.

entries.title: exceedingly.
entries.content: exceedingly. Figure of speech Epizeuxis ( greatly greatly) . App-6 .

entries.title: fell.
entries.content:
fell. Compare Mary (John 11:32 ) and contrast Martha (John 11:21 ).

God = Elohim , Creator. Used in this ch. (verses: Genesis 17:3 , Genesis 17:9 , Genesis 17:15 , Genesis 3:18 , Genesis 3:22 , Genesis 3:23 ) because He creates new names (verses: Genesis 17:5 , Genesis 17:15 ), a new Sign of Covenant (verses: Genesis 17:9-14 ), and a new thing, from one as good as dead (Hebrews 11:12 ).

entries.title: many.
entries.content: many. Emph. Figure of speech Antimereia (of Noun), for emphasis.

entries.title: Abraham.
entries.content: Abraham. The fifth letter of Hebrew alphabet (= H), put in middle of his name = No. 5, Grace. See App-10 . Abram = exalted father; Abraham = father of a multitude.

entries.title: exceeding.
entries.content:
exceeding. Figure of speech Epizeuxis ( greatly greatly) . App-6 .

nations. Abraham was the progenitor not only of Israel, but of Ishmaelites, Midianites, Arabians, &c.

entries.title: covenant:
entries.content:
covenant: unconditional.

thy seed. Here, the collective noun ser'a is shown to be plural by the words "after thee" (compare verses: Genesis 17:8 , Genesis 17:9 ), and by the plural pronoun "their generations" (verses: Genesis 17:7 , Genesis 17:9 ). This is not the verse referred to in Galatians 1:3 , Galatians 1:16 , but Genesis 21:12 . See note on Genesis 21:12 , where "seed" must be in the singular because of the verb.

everlasting. Hence Israel so called. Isaiah 44:7 margin.

entries.title: land . . . stranger.
entries.content: land . . . stranger. Hebrew. land of thy sojourning!

entries.title: thy seed.
entries.content: thy seed. Still practiced by Ishmaelites and others. Noncircumcision was the "reproach" of Egypt (Joshua 5:9 ).

entries.title: eight
entries.content: eight = the number of Resurrection ( App-10 ); associated here with circumcision, the sign of death.

entries.title: flesh.
entries.content: flesh. Figure of speech Synecdoche, for the whole person. App-6 .

entries.title: soul.
entries.content: soul. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 . Figure of speech Synecdoche, for person.

entries.title: Sarah.
entries.content: Sarah. The addition of the 5th letter (= H) of Hebrew alphabet (the No. of Grace, App-10 ) as in Abraham's case (Genesis 17:5 ) and Joshua's (Numbers 13:16 ). The letter (H) is common to both the names of Jehovah and Elohim. Sarai = princely; Sarah = princess.

entries.title: kings.
entries.content: kings. Samaritan Pentateuch, Targum of Onkelos, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, and Syriac read "and kings".

entries.title: laughed:
entries.content:
laughed: for joy. Hebrew. was joyful. Compare John 8:56 , "rejoiced to see my day . . . and was glad. "The laughter of faith, Romans 4:19 . Sarah did not fall down as Abraham did, Genesis 17:3 .

Shall, &c. Figure of speech Erotesis. (Compare Hebrews 11:12 ).

entries.title: might live,
entries.content: might live, as though he thought Ishmael was to die: showing his faith in Isaac's birth. This is proved from Genesis 17:20 .

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Samaritan Pentateuch, Targum of Onkelos, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, Syriac read this "and" in the text.

entries.title: I have heard.
entries.content:
I have heard. Showing the subject of Abraham's prayer.

exceedingly. Figure of speech Epizeuxis ( greatly greatly) .

entries.title: Isaac.
entries.content:
Isaac. Hebrew. laughter.

set time. See note on Genesis 1:14 .

entries.title: circumcised.
entries.content: circumcised. Hence Ishmaelites and kindred nations still practice the rite.

entries.title: thirteen.
entries.content: thirteen. Symbolic; and in contrast with Isaac on eighth day. See App-10 , Ishmaelites and Arabians still circumcise in the 13th year.

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

plains = among the oaks of Mamre. Compare Genesis 13:18 ; Genesis 14:13 , and Genesis 18:8 .

sat = was sitting.

entries.title: looked.
entries.content:
looked. See note on Genesis 13:14 .

lo. The Figure of speech Asterismos.

three men. Elohim ( App-4 ) and two angels called men (Hebrew. 'ish, plural, App-14 ) here, and verses: Genesis 18:16 , Genesis 18:22 , but in Genesis 19:1 , Genesis 19:15 the two are called "angels". Three the No. of Divine perfection (see App-10 ). "When two departed, Elohim (the Divine Presence) remained (verses: Genesis 18:16 , Genesis 18:22 ).

entries.title: LORD
entries.content: LORD = Jehovah, not Adonai. See App-32 . But plural throughout Genesis 19 of the two.

entries.title: wash your feet.
entries.content: wash your feet. A common practice to this day; needed from use of sandals and bare feet; Compare Genesis 24:32 ; Genesis 43:24 .

entries.title: bread.
entries.content: bread. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species), App-6 , put for food in general.

entries.title: three measures.
entries.content:
three measures. Note the No. 3. See Genesis 18:2 and App-10 .

cakes. Evidently unleavened.

entries.title: ran.
entries.content: ran. Such speedy hospitality common in the East.

entries.title: tree.
entries.content:
tree. See Genesis 18:1 .

eat. We do not understand this mystery. But we read of "angels' food" (Psalms 78:25 ); and that Christ ate after His resurrection (Luke 24:30 , Luke 24:43 .Acts 10:41; Acts 10:41 ).

entries.title: Where, &c.
entries.content: Where, &c. Translate "And as to Sarah thy wife . . . and he [interrupting] said, Lo! [she is] in the tent". See App-31 .

entries.title: certainly return.
entries.content:
certainly return. Figure of speech Polyptoton (returning I will return) for emphasis.

lo! Figure of speech Asterismos. App-6 . heard. Hebrew was listening.

entries.title: old.
entries.content: old. This explains how Rebekah, a granddaughter of Abraham's brother, should be old enough to marry Isaac, Abraham's son.

entries.title: laughed.
entries.content:
laughed. See note on Genesis 17:17 .

After. Figure of speech Erotesis.

my lord. Hebrew. Adon. See App-4 and compare 1 Peter 3:6 .

entries.title: Wherefore?
entries.content: Wherefore? Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 .

entries.title: Is any thing?
entries.content:
Is any thing? Figure of speech Erotesis.

hard = wonderful. A similar question and same Figure of speech used in Luke 1:37 .

time appointed. See note on Genesis 1:14 .

entries.title: looked
entries.content: looked = looked down upon. Hebrew. shakaph. First occurance.

entries.title: Shall I hide?
entries.content: Shall I hide? Figure of speech Erotesis. Compare Amos 3:7 .

entries.title: shall surely become.
entries.content:
shall surely become. Hebrew "being shall be". Figure of speech Polyptoton See note on Genesis 26:28 .

nations. Another proof that the mystery (Ephesians 3 ) means more than Gentile blessing. Compare Genesis 22:18 .

entries.title: that
entries.content:
that = how that.

command. Compare Psalms 78:1-8 .

entries.title: cry.
entries.content: cry. Figure of speech Prosopopoeia. App-6 .

entries.title: I will go down
entries.content:
I will go down = let us now go down. See Genesis 11:7 . Exodus 3:8 , all times of judgment.

the cry. Should be their outcry: with Septuagint, Targum of Onkelos, and ancient reading in MSS. called Sevir. See App-34 .

entries.title: the men.
entries.content:
the men. Probably the two of Genesis 19:1 .

Abraham stood yet before the LORD. The primitive text read "Jehovah stood yet before Abraham. "One of the 18 emendations of the Sopherim. See App-33 .

entries.title: also
entries.content:
also = even, or really. Note the 6 petitions in Abraham's prayer, verses: Genesis 18:24-32 . See App-10 .

wicked. Hebrew. rasha'. App-44 .

entries.title: Peradventure
entries.content: Peradventure = perhaps.

entries.title: earth.
entries.content: earth. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). App-6 . "Earth" put for its inhabitants

entries.title: LORD*.
entries.content:
LORD*. One of the 134 places where the Primitive Text was Jehovah, and the Sopherim changed it to Adonai. These are distinguished in the text by an asterisk, and printed LORD*. See list, App-32 .

dust and ashes. Figure of speech Meiosis. App-6 . Also Paronomasia (v'ephar 'aphar).

entries.title: went His way.
entries.content: went His way. The same as the one who came in verses: Genesis 18:1 , Genesis 18:2 .

entries.title: two.
entries.content:
two. Hebrew the two. With article, viz. two of the three, Genesis 18:16 .

Sodom = flaming, burning.

even. Note emph. on notes of time in the Structure.

gate. The seat of judgment, showing that Lot was a real citizen, Genesis 19:9 ; Genesis 23:10 , Genesis 23:18 ; Genesis 34:20 , Genesis 34:24 .Ruth 4:1 .

entries.title: my lords.
entries.content:
my lords. Plural of Adon.

in the street. Figure of speech Peristasis.

entries.title: eat.
entries.content: eat. See Genesis 18:8 .

entries.title: know.
entries.content: know. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). App-6 .

entries.title: known.
entries.content:
known. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause).

these. Archaic pronoun showing antiquity of Pentateuch

roof. Figure of speech Metalepsis. App-6 . Roof put for house, and house put for protection.

entries.title: judge.
entries.content:
judge. See Genesis 19:1 . He sat in Sodom's gate, the seat of the judges. See note on Genesis 13:7 .

worse. Hebrew. ra'. App-44 .

break = break open, shiver.

entries.title: blindness.
entries.content: blindness. Produced by dazzlings of light. Figure of speech Heterosis (of Noun). Plural put for sing, only here and 2 Kings 6:18 . 2 Kings 6:9 instances of people so smitten (see App-10 ). See Genesis 19:11 ; Genesis 27:1 ; Genesis 48:10 . Jdg 16:21 . 1 Samuel 4:15 . 1 Kings 14:4 . 2Ki 6:18 ; 2 Kings 25:7 . Acts 13:11 .

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton.

entries.title: will destroy
entries.content:
will destroy = are about to destroy.

face. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia. App-6 .

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Compare the "we" of Genesis 19:13 . Hebrew. Jehovah.

one that mocked. [ talked nonsense ] See notes on next page.

one that mocked = talked nonsense. He had looked, and pitched his tent toward Sodom, had dwelt and made his home there, and married his daughters, and sat in its gate as a judge. No wonder he seemed as one that mocked. He chose Sodom (Genesis 13:11 ), and "lingered" in the place of his choice (Genesis 19:16 ). See note, Genesis 13:7 .

entries.title: iniquity.
entries.content: iniquity. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). App-6 . Cause put for effect = judgment. Compare Psalms 7:16 .

entries.title: lingered.
entries.content: lingered. See Genesis 19:14 .

entries.title: He.
entries.content:
He. Septuagint reads "they".

life = soul. Hebrew. nephesh. See App-13 .

look, &c. Figure of speech Asyndeton. (No ands, but climax.)

entries.title: LORD*
entries.content: LORD* . see note on Genesis 18:27 .

entries.title: is it not a little one?
entries.content:
is it not a little one? Figure of speech Epitrechon.

my soul = myself. Hebrew my nephesh.

entries.title: thee.
entries.content: thee. Hebrew. thy face . Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Part).

entries.title: Zoar
entries.content: Zoar = little, or smallness. Compare Genesis 14:2 , Genesis 14:8 .

entries.title: the LORD . . . from the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD . . . from the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. Repetition very emphatic. Compare "we", Genesis 19:13 .

brimstone and fire. Figure of speech Hendiadys ( App-6 ) = burning brimstone. Referred to in Deuteronomy 29:23 .Isaiah 13:19 . Jeremiah 49:18 . Zephaniah 2:9 . Matthew 10:15 . 2 Peter 2:6 . Jude 1:7 .

entries.title: overthrew.
entries.content: overthrew. These cities are not in the Dead Sea, but their ruins have been discovered by M. de Saulcy (called to-day Kharbet-Goumran), about 4 miles square ( Journey round the Dead Sea, vol. ii, pp. 42-46). Note the parallelism ( Alternation ). a | cities. b | plain. a | cities (inhabitants). b | plain (produce).

entries.title: wife.
entries.content:
wife. Compare Luke 17:32 .

looked back: i.e. curiously. Compare Isaiah 63:5 and Genesis 19:28 . Same word as in Genesis 19:17 .

became. Same word as Genesis 1:2 , "the earth became. "

entries.title: stood.
entries.content: stood. Compare note on Genesis 18:22 .

entries.title: looked toward.
entries.content:
looked toward. A different word from Genesis 19:27 . Abraham bent forward and looked with awe and grief.

smoke. It does not say he saw the cities, but only the smoke.

entries.title: God.
entries.content:
God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

remembered. Lot's deliverance due to Abraham's prayer. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia.

cities = the city. Figure of speech Heterosis (of Number). App-6 .

entries.title: wine.
entries.content: wine. Hebrew. yayin. See App-27 .

entries.title: nor
entries.content: nor = but. This clause is one marked with the "fifteen extraordinary points" calling attention to the ancient readings "he did know when she arose. "See App-31 .

entries.title: Moab.
entries.content: Moab. Hebrew. from a father.

entries.title: Ben-ammi.
entries.content: Ben-ammi. Hebrew. son of Ammi = "the god Am". See on Genesis 14:5 and Deuteronomy 2:20 . Begotten in shame, both had a shameful history. Deuteronomy 23:3 , Deuteronomy 23:4 . Compare Judges 10:10 ; Judges 11:4 , Judges 11:15 .Numbers 21:29 . Deuteronomy 2:19 ; Deuteronomy 3:16 . 2 Chronicles 20:1 .

entries.title: south
entries.content: south = the Negeb. See Genesis 12:9 ; Genesis 13:1 .

entries.title: said.
entries.content:
said. Abraham's expedient = the next assault on Abraham in the Great Conflict for the destruction of the promised seed of the woman (Genesis 3:15 ). See App-23 . God had to intervene (Genesis 20:3 ), for man could know nothing of it. Abraham's fear shown in Genesis 20:11 .

my sister = half-sister. See note on Genesis 20:12 and App-29 .

Abimelech. Hebrew. Father-king. The official title of the kings of Gerar (Compare Genesis 26:1 ), like Pharaoh in Egypt.

took. See note on Genesis 21:7 . In Sarah's conception God must have renewed her youth, for she nursed Isaac (Genesis 21:7 ).

entries.title: dream.
entries.content:
dream. 20 recorded in Scripture (see App-10 ). Genesis 20:3 ; Genesis 28:12 ; Genesis 31:10 , Genesis 31:24 ; Genesis 37:5 , Genesis 37:9 ; Genesis 40:5 , Genesis 40:6 ; Genesis 41:1 , Genesis 41:5 , Genesis 41:5 .Judges 7:13 . 1 Kings 3:5 .Daniel 2:3 ; Daniel 4:5 ; Daniel 7:1 .Matthew 1:20 ; Matthew 2:12 , Matthew 2:13 , Matthew 2:19 ; Matthew 27:19 .

man . . . for. Figure of speech Aposiopesis, or "sudden silence". We must supply "If thou dost not restore her"; or "I will slay thee". See verses: Genesis 20:4 and Genesis 20:7 .

entries.title: LORD*
entries.content:
LORD* = Jehovah. One of the 134 emendations of the Sopherim. See App-32 .

also, i.e. as well as Sodom and Gomorrah, Genesis 19 .

nation. Abimelech evidently expected God to slay the whole nation.

entries.title: I also withheld.
entries.content:
I also withheld. Divine intervention needed. Compare Genesis 20:2 . Note the emphatic pronouns. See App-23 .

sinning. See App-44 .

touch. Here is the Hebrew word naga = touch, used in a clear understandable sense as it is used in Genesis 3:3 , "neither shall ye touch it". See note on Genesis 3:3 .

entries.title: prophet.
entries.content: prophet. First occ, showing that prediction is only a small part of its meaning = God's spokesman. Here, it is prayer (compare Exodus 4:16 with Exodus 7:1 ), and prayer is associated with prophesying, i.e. witnessing (1 Corinthians 11:5 ).

entries.title: What.
entries.content:
What. Figure of speech Aganactesis.

sin. Hebrew. chat'a. See App-44 .

entries.title: sawest thou
entries.content: sawest thou = hadst thou seen.

entries.title: thought.
entries.content:
thought. Hebrew. said : i.e. said [to myself ].

slay me. Showing how his fears were worked upon by the enemy. See Genesis 20:2 .

entries.title: sister.
entries.content: sister. The daughter of Terah by another wife (than Abraham's mother): therefore, Abraham's half-sister. See App-29 .

entries.title: caused.
entries.content: caused. The verb is in the plural. kindness. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). Kindness put for the kind deeds caused by it.

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Figure of speech Polysyndeton. App-6 .

entries.title: brother.
entries.content:
brother. Figure of speech Irony.

covering, &c. Figure of speech Periphrasis. App-6 . Having called Abraham her "brother", he uses this beautiful Figure for her husband. Compare Genesis 24:65 . 1 Corinthians 11:5 , &c.

reproved, i.e. by the Irony.

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

as = according as.

said. Emphasis on "said" for our faith.

spoken. Figure of speech Pleonasm ( App-6 ), for emphasis.

entries.title: set time
entries.content:
set time = exact time.

God. Hebrew. Elohim. Note change of title here, till Genesis 21:32 , because it is Creator and creature. In Genesis 21:33 , Jehovah, where it is Covenant relation. In Mary's song both titles united (Luke 1:46 , Luke 1:47 and compare verses: Gen 21:37 , Gen 21:38 ).

entries.title: Isaac.
entries.content: Isaac. Hebrew. Let him laugh. Compare Genesis 17:17 ; Genesis 18:12 , Genesis 18:13 , Genesis 18:15 ; Genesis 21:6 , Genesis 21:9 ; Genesis 26:8 .

entries.title: eight.
entries.content: eight. The Dominical No. See App-10 . Compare Ishmael, 13th year.

entries.title: hundred.
entries.content: hundred. See App-10 .

entries.title: suck.
entries.content: suck. A proof that "God", the Creator, had renewed her youth, showing why Abimelech should have taken her (Genesis 20:2 ). Sarah's Magnificat may be compared with Mary's. The scenes of both near to each other. Mary's words (Luke 1:54 , Luke 1:55 ) connect her "mercy" with that shown to "Abraham and his seed",

entries.title: grew.
entries.content: grew. Compare Luke 2:40 .

entries.title: mocking.
entries.content: mocking. Hebrew "laughing" or "chaffing", or "mocking again" (as we say).

entries.title: Cast out, &c.
entries.content:
Cast out, &c. See the Divine interpretation. Galatians 1:3 , Gal 1:6-29 ; Galatians 4:22-31 .

with my son, &c Hebrew idiom "with my son with Isaac". Compare Numbers 12:8 .

entries.title: thing.
entries.content: thing. Hebrew. word.

entries.title: Isaac . . . thy seed.
entries.content: Isaac . . . thy seed. Here ser'a is in the sing sense, because of the word "Isaac", and because of the sing verb "it shall be called. " Zer'a is a collective noun (like Eng. "sheep"), but the context must determine whether it is sing, or plural. It is to this verse Galatians 1:3 , Galatians 1:16 refers; not to Genesis 12:7 , where it is indefinite; or Genesis 17:7 where the verb and pronouns show it is plural. See note there, and on Galatians 1:3 , Galatians 1:16 ; and compare Romans 9:7 . Hebrews 11:18 . "Thy seed" is therefore "Christ". The difference of the 30 years comes in here: 430 to the Exodus ( Gen 12:40 ) from Genesis 12:4 , when Abraham was 75: 25 thence to Isaac's birth: and now, 5 to his recognition as the seed = 30 years.

entries.title: bottle.
entries.content:
bottle. Compare man's provision (a bottle) with God's (a well) (Genesis 21:19 ).

it. Hagar put the "bottle of water" on her shoulder, surely not Ishmael, because Ishmael was about seventeen years old at this time. Abraham was Eighty-six years of age when Ishmael was born (Genesis 16:16 ), Isaac was born when Abraham was one-hundred years old (Genesis 21:6 ), then Ishmael would have been fourteen-years old when Isaac was born, Add to the age of Isaac when he was weaned (Genesis 21:8 ) three years.

entries.title: lift up her voice
entries.content: lift up her voice = the boy lifted tip his voice and wept. So Septuagint (see Genesis 21:17 ).

entries.title: heard.
entries.content: heard. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia. App-6 .

entries.title: well.
entries.content: well. Hebrew. beer, a well (digged): not 'ayin, a spring or fountain; or bor , a cistern (hewn).

entries.title: kindness.
entries.content: kindness. Fig, Metonymy (of Cause). App-6 . See Genesis 20:13 .

entries.title: violently, &c.
entries.content: violently, &c. Compare Genesis 26:19 , Genesis 26:20 . Exodus 2:17 . Judges 5:11 . This explains Exodus 17:8 , "Then came Amalek", because of verses: Genesis 21:1-7 .

entries.title: wot not
entries.content: wot not = know not. O. Eng. idiom.

entries.title: both.
entries.content:
both. Not one party as in Genesis 15:10-18 . Compare Galatians 3:20 .

made. Hebrew. cut, because of the dividing of the sacrifice. Compare Genesis 15:10 . Jeremiah 34:18-20 . Eng. concluded or solemnized.

entries.title: Beer-sheba
entries.content: Beer-sheba = Hebrew. well of the oath.

entries.title: grove.
entries.content:
grove. Hebrew. 'eshel = trees, riot 'asherah ( App-42 ), but the wood for Genesis 22:3 about twenty years later.

the everlasting GOD. This is the Divine definition of Jehovah (Lord), Hebrew. 'olam = duration, secret and hidden from man. Compare Psalms 90:2 .

entries.title: God.
entries.content:
God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

after, i.e. after 40 or 50 years in Canaan.

tempt. Hebrew. prove, so Exodus 15:25 ; Exodus 16:4 ; Exodus 20:20 . Deuteronomy 8:2 , Deuteronomy 8:16 . Judges 2:22 ; Judges 3:1 , Judges 3:4 .Ecclesiastes 2:1 ; Ecc 7:23 . 1 Samuel 17:39 . 1 Kings 10:1 , &c. Compare Deuteronomy 4:34 (assayed). In later usage trial meant trouble. Book of Wisdom 3.5; 11.10. Sir. 2.1. Judith 8:24-27. Luke 8:13 (compare Matthew 13:21 ). Acts 20:19 . Heb 2:18 . 1 Peter 1:6 .

Behold, &c. = behold me.

entries.title: lovest.
entries.content:
lovest. Note the reference to the Antitype.

Moriah. Hebrew = shown or provided by Jah. Compare 1 Chronicles 21:22 ; 1Ch 22:1 . 2 Chronicles 3:1 . Christ crucified also on one of these mountains. Matthew 27:33 .

offer. Hebrew. 'alah. See App-43 .

burnt offering. Hebrew. 'olah.

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton , emphasizing the calmness of Abraham's deliberate faith. Each "and" is to be noted, and each act weighed.

entries.title: the third day.
entries.content: the third day. No. 3. Symb. of resurrection ( App-10 ). Compare Genesis 22:5 , "Come again, "1st pers. Plural. Exactly 3 days journey from Beer-sheba to Moriah. Gerizim Isaiah 2 days further.

entries.title: I and the lad.
entries.content:
I and the lad. This is polite Hebrew, while "the lad and I" would be polite English.

yonder. Hebrew. as far as there (as though pointing).

come again. This was proof of Abraham's faith. 1st pers. plural, "We will come again. "

entries.title: laid.
entries.content:
laid. Compare John 19:17 .

fire. Without doubt fire from Abraham's own altar (Genesis 12:7 ; Genesis 13:4 , Genesis 13:18 ; and see note on Genesis 21:33 ), for God accepted a sacrifice only by fire from heaven. See on Genesis 4:4 .

both of them together. Compare the Father and the Son in the antitype. Emph. by repetition in Genesis 22:8 . John 10:30 ; John 14:10 , John 14:11 ; John 16:33 . The sinner is not seen in the type; his part is subsequent to this, viz. to believe what the Father and the Son have done for him in substitution. See also Romans 8:32 .

entries.title: Here, &c.
entries.content: Here, &c. Hebrew Behold me, my son.

entries.title: provide.
entries.content:
provide. Hebrew. yireh = God will see or look out

Himself = for Himself.

a lamb. Hebrew the lamb.

entries.title: and.
entries.content:
and. Each act is emph. by the Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ), and is to be dwelt upon and considered.

an altar. Hebrew the altar.

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah.

Abraham . . .Abraham. Figure of speech Epizeuxis ( App-6 ), for emphasis. Compare the 10 Duplications: (1) Seven used by God to men: Genesis 22:11 ; Genesis 46:2 .Exodus 3:4 . 1 Samuel 3:10 . Luke 10:41 ; Luke 22:31 .Acts 9:4 ; (2) Three under other circumstances: Matthew 7:21 , Matthew 7:22 (Luke 6:46 ; Luke 13:25 ), Matthew 23:37 (Luke 13:34 ). Mark 15:34 (Matthew 27:46 . Psalms 22:1 ).

entries.title: lifted up his eyes.
entries.content:
lifted up his eyes. Figure of speech Pleonasm, for emph, ( App-6 ).

looked. See note on Genesis 13:14 .

behold. Figure of speech Asterismos.

a ram. Some Codices (with Samaritan Pentateuch, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, and Syriac) read "one ram", i.e. a solitary ram.

a thicket. Hebrew the thicket.

in the stead. Here is the doctrine of substitution, clearly stated.

entries.title: Jehovah-jireh.
entries.content:
Jehovah-jireh. Hebrew. Jehovah will see, or provide, as in Genesis 22:8 . See App-4 .

In the mount, &c. Figure of speech Paroemia.

it shall be seen: it will be provided, or "in the mount Jehovah will be seen". So it was in 2 Samuel 24:25 . 1 Chronicles 21:26 . 2 Chronicles 7:1-3 .

entries.title: the second time.
entries.content: the second time. Hebrew a second time; the first time was for substitution; the second was for revelation.

entries.title: sworn.
entries.content: sworn. This oath is the foundation of Israel's blessings (Genesis 24:7 ; Genesis 26:3 ; Genesis 50:24 .Exodus 13:5 , Exodus 13:11 ; Exodus 33:1 ). David's "sure mercies" all grounded on it (Psalms 89:35 ; Psalms 132:11 . Compare Luke 1:73 ).

entries.title: blessing I will bless
entries.content:
blessing I will bless = I will surely bless; or, I will richly bless. Figure of speech Polyptoton ( App-6 ), for emphasis.

stars . . . sand, &c. Figure of speech Parozmia. See note on Genesis 13:16 .

the gate. Figure of speech Sy n e cd o c h e (ofthe Part), App-6 . "Gate" put for the cities.

entries.title: all the nations.
entries.content: all the nations. Proof that the "Mystery" does not mean blessing of Gentiles as such: but the secret concerning Christ and the church (Ephesians 5:32 ).

entries.title: these eight.
entries.content: these eight. Nahor had 12 in all, as Ishmael had (Genesis 25:13-16 ), and as Jacob had (Genesis 35:23-27 ).

entries.title: Maachah.
entries.content: Maachah. See Deuteronomy 3:14 .Joshua 12:5 . 2 Samuel 10:6 .

entries.title: Sarah.
entries.content: Sarah. The only woman whose age is mentioned in the Bible. in Genesis 22:23 Rebekah is mentioned: one sun rising before the other sets.

entries.title: Kirjath-arba.
entries.content: Kirjath-arba. See notes on Numbers 13:22 , and App-25 .

entries.title: before his dead.
entries.content: before his dead. Heb leaning over the face of his dead. Figure of speech Pleonasm.

entries.title: I am.
entries.content:
I am. Compare "thou art", Genesis 23:6 .

stranger and a sojourner. Compare 1 Peter 2:11 .Psalms 39:12 .

entries.title: children.
entries.content: children. Hebrew. sons, and so elsewhere.

entries.title: mighty prince.
entries.content: mighty prince. Hebrew. prince of El. Genitive of relation ( App-17 ), for Adjective. Compare Psalms 36:7 ; Psalms 80:10 .

entries.title: mind
entries.content: mind = soul. Hebrew. nephesh, App-13 .

entries.title: money
entries.content:
money . Hebrew silver.

buryingplace. What Jacob bought (Genesis 33:19 , Genesis 33:20 ) was for an altar.

entries.title: dwelt.
entries.content: dwelt. Hebrew was sitting there.

entries.title: give I.
entries.content: give I. Hebrew have I given. Figure of speech Antimereia (of Verb), past for present.

entries.title: wilt give.
entries.content: wilt give. Figure of speech Ellipsis. Supply "hast given" from Genesis 23:11 .

entries.title: what is that.
entries.content: what is that. Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 .

entries.title: Abraham.
entries.content:
Abraham. This is not the purchase referred to in Genesis 33:19 and Acts 7:16 . Act 7:80 years between this purchase and Jacob's. See note on Acts 7:16 .

before all. Some Codices with Samaritan Pentateuch have "even before all".

entries.title: made sure.
entries.content:
made sure. This was all strictly in conformity with the commercial enactments of the Code of Khammurabi. See App-15 .

buryingplace. All that Abraham possessed; hut in the faith and hope of resurrection.

entries.title: old.
entries.content:
old. About 140 years old.

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

entries.title: eldest servant.
entries.content:
eldest servant. Probably Eleazar of Dan 15:2 .

thigh. According to the Midrash and ancient Jewish expositors, a Euphemism ( App-6 ) for the organs of generation, as most sacred. According to Ibn Ezra and present Indian custom, on the thigh is a token of subjection.

entries.title: God.
entries.content:
God. Hebrew. Elohim .

Canaanites. Mixed with the Nephilim. App-23 .

I. Emph. in contrast with the Canaanites. Hence Abraham's horror of mixing the holy seed with that of the Nephilim.

entries.title: my kindred.
entries.content: my kindred. Gentiles thus expressly excluded from this chapter, if regarded as a type. Compare verses: Genesis 24:3 , Genesis 24:4 , Genesis 24:7 , Gen 3:37 , Gen 3:38 . See also Genesis 26:35 ; Genesis 27:46 ; Genesis 28:1 , Genesis 28:8 .

entries.title: heaven.
entries.content:
heaven. The Septuagint reads: "heaven, and God of the earth. "See App-4 .

father's house, and from the land of my kindred. The Severus Codex reads: "from my house and from my country, "as in Genesis 24:4 . See App-34 .

entries.title: arose
entries.content:
arose = amounted.

Mesopotamia Hebrew. Aram-naharaim, i.e. Aram of the two rivers (the Tigris and Euphrates). The country of Haran. Genesis 11:31 .

entries.title: well
entries.content:
well = spring. Hebrew. 'ayin. See note on Genesis 21:19 .

come out. Hebrew are coming out.

entries.title: pitcher.
entries.content: pitcher. Still used in Palestine as in John 4:28 .

entries.title: before he had done speaking.
entries.content:
before he had done speaking. Compare Isaiah 65:24 .

Rebekah. Hebrew captivating.

born to Bethuel. See App-29 .

Bethuel. Hebrew separated of God.

entries.title: virgin.
entries.content: virgin. Hebrew. bethulah. Compare Genesis 24:43 . See note on Genesis 24:43 .

entries.title: wondering:
entries.content:
wondering: or eagerly watching her.

to wit = to know.

entries.title: golden.
entries.content:
golden. Hebrew of gold. Genitive of material. App-17 .

earring. Probably a nose (or "face") ring. See Genesis 24:47 .

entries.title: Nahor.
entries.content: Nahor. See App-29 . Rebekah his granddaughter; but old enough to marry Isaac, because Sarah was "well stricken in years" when Isaac was born (Genesis 18:11 , Genesis 18:12 ). Compare Genesis 24:36 .

entries.title: Laban.
entries.content: Laban. See App-29 .

entries.title: when he saw.
entries.content: when he saw. Characteristic of Laban. Rebekah showed kindness before she saw.

entries.title: he,
entries.content: he, i.e. Laban.

entries.title: And.
entries.content: And. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton, App-6 , to emphasize all the items which went to make up Abraham's wealth. Twelve "ands" (3 x 4 = 12) = abundance of earthly wealth. See App-10 .

entries.title: I walk
entries.content: I walk = I walk habitually. Hebrew verb in Hithpael.

entries.title: said.
entries.content: said. Eleazar repeats his prayer from memory, but inexactly. Who could have written the actual words (verses: Genesis 24:12-21 ) but the Holy Inspiring Spirit? He records both the prayer itself and Eleazar's remembrance of it.

entries.title: virgin.
entries.content: virgin. Hebrew. 'almah. Every bethulah is an 'ahnah, but every 'almah is not a bethulah : 'almah Occurs 7 times, Genesis 24:43 (first occurance). Exodus 2:8 . Psalms 68:25 .Proverbs 30:19 . Song of Solomon 1:3 ; Song of Solomon 6:8 . Isaiah 7:14 . Bethulah Occurs 49 times ( App-10 ).

entries.title: face
entries.content: face or nose. Compare Genesis 24:22 .

entries.title: led me in the right way.
entries.content:
led me in the right way. Compare Psalms 107:7 .

daughter. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Species), App-6 , daughter put for granddaughter.

entries.title: raiment:
entries.content: raiment: or garments; i.e. changes of raiment.

entries.title: ten.
entries.content: ten. Seven days = a week, but ten or a decad (1/3 of a month) sometimes reckoned as a longer, but strictly defined period. Compare Exodus 12:3 .Leviticus 16:29 .

entries.title: well
entries.content:
well = spring. Hebrew. beer. See note on Genesis 21:19 .

Lahai-roi. Hebrew. the well of life and vision.

entries.title: meditate.
entries.content: meditate. Refers back to the historical context, Genesis 23:19 , the death and burial of Sarah, his mother. What follows this digression (of which Isaac as yet knew nothing) in Genesis 24:1-67 shows that Isaac went out, not to "meditate", or "to pray" (Authorized Version margin), or "take a walk" (Syriac), or "muster the flocks" (Gesenius), but to mourn. This is the meaning of the Hebrew suach. in Psalms 44:25 .Lamentations 3:20 .

entries.title: lighted off.
entries.content: lighted off. Hebrew. fell, or alighted hastily.

entries.title: comforted after,
entries.content: comforted after, or consoled himself for.

entries.title: a wife
entries.content:
This genealogy, and Abraham's death recorded here, because no more is to be said about Abraham. Abraham, however, lived until Jacob was 15. Shem died 1846.

a wife = another, instead of "again".

entries.title: Medan
entries.content:
Medan and

Midian were half-brothers with Ishmael, and they were mixed up together in their dealings. See note on Genesis 37:25 , Genesis 37:28 .

entries.title: these
entries.content: these = the tares, sown after Isaac, the good seed.
175 years. Therefore a sojourner 100 years. Compare Genesis 12:4 .

entries.title: full of.
entries.content:
full of. Hebrew "satisfied with". Supply "days" (not "years"), with Samaritan Pentateuch, Targum of Onkelos, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, and Syriac.

gathered to his people, an idiomatic Euphemism ( App-6 ) for death and burial. Abraham's "people" were idolaters (Joshua 24:2 ). See note on 2 Samuel 12:23 .

entries.title: Machpelah.
entries.content: Machpelah. Compare Genesis 23:9 .

entries.title: purchased.
entries.content: purchased. Compare Genesis 23:16 .

entries.title: God.
entries.content:
God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

well. Hebrew. beer. See note on Genesis 21:19 .

Lahai-roi. Compare Genesis 16:14 ; Genesis 24:62 .

entries.title: died
entries.content: died = had inheritance. Heb, naphal, to fall, esp. as a lot, giving inheritance (Judges 18:1 . 1 Chronicles 1:20 ; 1Ch 26:14 . 2 Chronicles 15:9 . Psalms 16:6 (compare Joshua 23:4 . Hebrew caused the lot to fall). Hence, to dwell with, as in Proverbs 1:14 . Compare Judges 7:12 , to encamp, lying along the ground. Ishmael was to dwell in the presence (Hebrew "on the face") of his brethren, i.e. mixed up with them (Genesis 16:12 ). See Genesis 37:25 , Genesis 37:28 , Genesis 37:36 ; Genesis 39:1 , and compare Judges 8:24 . Midian, being his half-brother (Genesis 15:11 , Genesis 15:12 ). Naphal never rendered "die" elsewhere.

entries.title: begat.
entries.content: begat. The same form of the verb as in Genesis 5 , used of the godly seed.

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content: the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

entries.title: heel.
entries.content: heel. Hebrew. yakob, whence the name Jacob ( yakob ) heel-catcher: hence, contender.

entries.title: cunning
entries.content:
cunning = knowing or skilled in.

a man of the field. "The field is the world. "

plain = upright or pure. Job 1:1 , Job 1:8 ; Job 2:3 , &c.

entries.title: venison.
entries.content: venison. Heb . hunting. Figure of speech Metonymy (of the Cause), App-6 , hunting put for what was caught. Eating was strong in Esau too (Genesis 25:34 ). It was "the will of the flesh" which Isaac's faith overcame in Genesis 27 , for he wished to bless Esau, and he loved his savoury meat, See note on Genesis 27:3 , Genesis 27:4 . Compare Hebrews 11:20 .

entries.title: sod.
entries.content:
sod. Part, of O Eng. verb seethe, to boil.

pottage = anything cooked in a pot.

entries.title: red.
entries.content:
red. Hebrew red red. Figure of speech Epizeuxis ( App-6 ). (No superlative in Hebrew) Figure of speech = th at delicious red [food].

Lentiles. See Genesis 25:34 .

Edom = Hebrew. red, ruddy. A reference also to Genesis 25:25 .

entries.title: this day.
entries.content:
this day. Hebrew "as on this very day. "Figure of speech Simile. App-6 . Compare Luke 23:43 .

birthright. Included (1) the Father's blessing and supremacy (which went to Jacob, Genesis 27 , and Genesis 49:8 . 1 Chronicles 5:1 , 1 Chronicles 5:2 ); (2) a double portion (which went to Joseph, Genesis 48 ; 1 Chronicles 5:1 , 1 Chronicles 5:2 ); and (3) the Domestic Priesthood (which after going to the firstborn of each family was vested in Levi for the whole nation. Numbers 3:6 , Numbers 3:12 . Compare Numbers 16:1-3 ).

entries.title: me.
entries.content: me. Figure of speech Ellipsis ( App-6 ) = Brachyology. The words to be supplied are "I will sell it". A famine accounts for the sale. See Genesis 26:1 .

entries.title: day.
entries.content:
day. Figure of speech Brachyology. App-6 . Supply "that thou wilt sell it".

birthright. The Severus Codex here reads "ware", i.e. Esau treated his birthright as merchandise. See App-34 .

entries.title: and.
entries.content:
and. Figure of speech Polysyndeton . Four "ands" marking the deliberateness of Esau's acts, and their solemn significance. He despised grace. See App-10 .

despised. Hence in Hebrews 12:16 he is called "a profane person".

entries.title: famine.
entries.content:
famine. Accounts for Esau's despair of living, and hence selling his birthright. Genesis 25:29-34 .

first. One of the thirteen famines. See note on Genesis 12:10 .

Abimelech = official name. Not the same as Genesis 20:2 .

entries.title: Go not down
entries.content: Go not down (as Abraham did, Genesis 12:10 ).

entries.title: Unto thee.
entries.content: Unto thee. So to each Patriarch: Abraham (Genesis 13:15 ), Jacob (Genesis 28:13 , &c), involving resurrection. See note on Genesis 50:24 , and Matthew 22:23-33 .

entries.title: stars.
entries.content: stars. Figure of speech Paroemia. App-6 .

entries.title: My.
entries.content:
My. Repeated 5 times for emphasis. The No. of Grace. See App-10

voice, to be heard and believed (Romans 10:17 ).

charge, to be observed.

commandments, to he obeyed.

statutes, i.e. decrees, to be acknowledged.

laws, i.e. instructions to be followed.

entries.title: he said.
entries.content:
he said. As Abraham had said (Genesis 12:13 ; Genesis 20:2 , Genesis 20:12 ).

sister. See note on Genesis 20:12 .

entries.title: sporting with,
entries.content: sporting with, or caressing

entries.title: What . . . ?
entries.content:
What . . . ? Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 .

guiltiness. See App-15 and App-44 .

entries.title: saying.
entries.content: saying. One of the Laws given and observed before Moses.

entries.title: received.
entries.content: received. Hebrew found. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Species). Compare Genesis 6:8 . Romans 4:1 .

entries.title: store
entries.content: store = body.

entries.title: in the days of Abraham his father.
entries.content:
in the days of Abraham his father. Isaac a placid character; shown by his obedience (Genesis 22:6 , Genesis 22:8 ), his meekness in betrothal (24), his mourning for his mother (Genesis 24:63-67 ; compare note on Gen 26:63 ), his following in his father's steps to Gerar (Genesis 20:1 ) in denying his wife there (20), his finding an Abimelech and Phichol there, and digging wells there, renewing the oath and renaming the well.

their names. Compare the four names below and their special meaning.

entries.title: well.
entries.content:
well. Hebrew. 'ayin. See note on Genesis 21:19 .

springing. Hebrew living. See note on Genesis 21:19 .

entries.title: Esek.
entries.content: Esek. Hebrew strife or contention.

entries.title: Sitnah.
entries.content: Sitnah. Hebrew opposition.

entries.title: Rehoboth.
entries.content: Rehoboth. Hebrew roominess.

entries.title: Beer-sheba.
entries.content: Beer-sheba. Hebrew the well of the oath.

entries.title: God.
entries.content: God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

entries.title: Phichol
entries.content: Phichol Probably an official military title. Compare Genesis 21:22 .

entries.title: saw certainly.
entries.content: saw certainly. Figure of speech Polyptoton ( App-6 ), for emphasis. Hebrew "seeing we saw". Compare Genesis 2:16 " freely eat"; Genesis 27:30 " scarce gone out"; Genesis 43:3 " solemnly protest"; Genesis 43:7 "asked us straitly ", "could we certainly know"; Genesis 43:20 "came indeed down"; Exodus 5:23 "not delivered us at all "; Genesis 18:18 "wilt surely wear away"; Genesis 21:5 "shall plainly say"; Job 37:2 "hear attentively "; Numbers 22:17 , Numbers 22:37 "promote thee to very great honour" = honouring I will honour thee; Genesis 24:10 " altogether blessed", Hebrew "blessing thou hast blessed". Numbers 26:65 ; Numbers 30:12 " utterly destroyed"; Genesis 23:11 ; Genesis 24:10 " altogether blessed".

entries.title: touched.
entries.content: touched. Figure of speech Tapeinosis. App-6 . Emphasizing the fact that so far from injuring him in any way they had shown him favour.

entries.title: Shebah.
entries.content:
Shebah. Hebrew an oath.

therefore. Same name given by Abraham (Genesis 21:31 ). Names were sometimes reimposed for a new reason. Compare Bethel (Genesis 28:18 , Genesis 28:19 with Genesis 35:6 , Genesis 35:7 ) and Israel (Genesis 32:28 with Genesis 35:10 ).

entries.title: Judith,
entries.content:
These names exhibit the Figure of speech. Polynyrmia. App-6 .

Judith, She had a second name, Aholibamah (Genesis 36:5 , Genesis 36:14 , Genesis 36:25 ).

Beeri. His name was also Anah, but he had acquired the name "Beeri" (or the spring-man) from his having discovered the hot springs. See on Genesis 36:24 .

Hittite = the general name. See note on 1 Kings 10:29 .

Bashematti had a second name, Adah. The name Bashemath dropped in Genesis 36:2 to avoid confusion with the daughter of Ishmael. In Genesis 26 : we have general history, but in Genesis 36 precise genealogy.

entries.title: grief.
entries.content:
grief. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Effect), grief put for that which caused it. No wonder it caused "bitterness of spirit" when we remember who the Canaanites were.

mind = spirit. Hebrew. ruach. See App-9 .

entries.title: old.
entries.content:
old. About 137 years (same age as his brother Ishmael died at). He recovered and lived 43 years longer (Compare Genesis 35:28 ).

Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos. App-6 .

entries.title: take me some venison.
entries.content: take me some venison. Hebrew hunt me some hunting. Figure of speech Polyptoton, and Metonymy (of Cause), by which venison, the result of hunting, is put for the hunting itself (from Latin venatio, a hunting). In Genesis 25:29 Esau missed his venison and lost his birthright. Was he now to miss it again and lose his blessing?

entries.title: such as I love.
entries.content:
such as I love. See verses: Genesis 27:27 , Genesis 27:9 , Genesis 27:14 and Genesis 25:28 .

my soul = myself. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

bless thee. He must have heard that he was to bless Jacob, for it was "by faith" he ultimately did so (Hebrews 11:20 ); and it came "by hearing" (Romans 10:17 ). "The will of the flesh" made him wish to bless Esau (Compare Genesis 27:4 with Genesis 25:28 ). But his faith in the end overcame "the will of the flesh" in him.

entries.title: heard.
entries.content:
heard. Hebrew was listening.

spake. Hebrew was speaking

entries.title: seem.
entries.content: seem. He shrinks, not from the fraud, but from its detection.

entries.title: goodly.
entries.content:
goodly. Hebrew desires. Figure of speech Metonymy (of the Adjunct), App-6 , put for the things desired or coveted (2 Chronicles 36:10 . Isaiah 64:11 .Lamentations 1:10; Lamentations 1:10 ).

raiment. All raiment in the East to this day marks the social rank and position of the wearer. Among the Bedouins, the chief and his eldest son wear a distinctive garment. This accounts for Jacob's desire here, and his act with Joseph (Genesis 37:3 ). Being the garment of the firstborn it doubtless denoted also his official and priestly position. Here, Hebrew. beged (compare Exodus 28:2 , Exodus 28:4 ; Exodus 35:19 . Leviticus 10:6 ; Leviticus 21:10 ), used of sacred things. Not the word rendered clothes in Deuteronomy 29:5 . No wonder Esau is called "profane" when he sold this his birthright (Hebrews 12:16 ).

entries.title: I am.
entries.content:
I am. Said perhaps because he had bought the birthright.

thy soul = thou. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

entries.title: wine
entries.content: wine = Hebrew. yayin. See App-27 .

entries.title: now.
entries.content: now. Not an adverb of time, but an expletive in command, emphasising the solemnity of the command. It must have been at this point that Isaac's faith overcame "the will of the flesh", and made him resolve to bless Jacob, in spite of it.

entries.title: corn.
entries.content:
corn. Put by Metonymy (of the Cause), App-6 , for bread and solid food generally. Compare Lamentations 2:12 .

wine. Hebrew. tirosh. See App-27 . Usually combined with "corn", as put by Metonymy (of the Cause) for all liquids.

entries.title: people.
entries.content: people. Hebrew peoples.

entries.title: scarce gone out.
entries.content: scarce gone out. Hebrew "going was gone". Figure of speech Polyptoton, for emph.; well represented by the word "scarce". See note on Genesis 26:28 .

entries.title: thy firstborn.
entries.content: thy firstborn. Esau still claims what he had sold.

entries.title: trembled very exceedingly.
entries.content:
trembled very exceedingly. The Figure of speech Polyptoton is thus beautifully rendered, Hebrew "trembled a great trembling greatly. "See note on. Genesis 26:28 . This trembling was not from doubt, or from the discovery (now made, verses: Genesis 27:26 , Genesis 27:27 ), but on account of the difficulty into which it had brought him with a man of Esau's temperament.

Jacob. See on Genesis 25:21 .

supplanted. Jacobed or over-reached me. See note on Genesis 25:26 with Genesis 32:28 .

blessing. This "blessing" is the "it" of Hebrews 12:17 .

entries.title: thy lord
entries.content:
thy lord = a mighty man unto thee. See App-14 . Fulfilled in 2 Samuel 8:14 .

wine. See note on Genesis 27:28 above.

entries.title: wept.
entries.content: wept. See Hebrews 12:17 , but could not change his father's mind.

entries.title: the fatness of the earth, and of.
entries.content: the fatness of the earth, and of. Hebrew of the fatness, &c. The "of", which is omitted in the first clause, is the preposition, which means "from". Revised Version margin away from. Compare Isaiah 22:3 .Jeremiah 48:33 .Lamentations 4:9 . Should be "Far from the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling, and far from the dew of the heavens, "&c. Jacob had already received the blessing "of" the fatness of the earth or the land (Genesis 27:28 ). Esau's was to be far from it, in the desert; and so it was.

entries.title: serve.
entries.content:
serve. See 1 Samuel 14:47 . 2Sa 8:14 . 2 Kings 8:20 , and compare 1 Kings 22:47 .

thou shalt break. Fulfilled in 2 Kings 8:20 , 2 Kings 8:22 .

entries.title: at hand.
entries.content: at hand. Isaac mistaken, verses: Genesis 27:1 , Genesis 27:2 . Esau mistaken here.

entries.title: flee thou.
entries.content:
flee thou. Hebrew flee for thyself.

Haran. See Genesis 11:31 .

entries.title: a few days.
entries.content:
a few days. Rebekah mistaken, for he was there 20 years.

Until. Figure of speech Synonymia.

entries.title: why. ?
entries.content:
why. ? Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 .

both. Jacob by Esau's hand, and Esau by the avenger of blood. Genesis 9:6 .

entries.title: daughters of Heth.
entries.content:
daughters of Heth. Refers to Esau's wives. Genesis 26:34 , Genesis 26:35 .

what good. Figure of speech Erotesis, and Figure of speech Aposiopesis, App-6 , Literally "Wherefore to me life? "Eng. Idiom, "What good would my life be to me? "

entries.title: blessed.
entries.content:
blessed. This blessing God endorses (verses: Genesis 28:13-15 ), by sending Jacob to Haran, as he had blessed Abraham to bring him from Haran (Genesis 12:1-3 ).

Thou shalt not take. See Genesis 24:3 .

entries.title: Padan-arain
entries.content: Padan-arain the plain of Syria.

entries.title: And.
entries.content:
And. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton in verses: Gen 28:28 , Genesis 28:3 and Genesis 28:4 ( App-6 ), marking 4 items in blessing. See App-10 .

GOD ALMIGHTY. EI Shaddai. See App-4 .

multitude: or convocation. Hebrew. kahal. First occurance. Occurs 123 times: rendered "multitude" 3, "assembly" 17, "congregation" 86, "company" 17. "Compare Genesis 49:6 . Psalms 22:22 , Psalms 22:25 .

people. Hebrew peoples.

entries.title: wherein thou art a stranger.
entries.content:
wherein thou art a stranger. Hebrew of thy sojournings.

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

entries.title: and.
entries.content:
and. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton , emphasizing (verses: Genesis 28:6-8 ) the effort of Esau to note what would please his parents.

Canaan. Compare Genesis 24:3 , and remember who these Canaanites were. See note on Genesis 12:6 .

entries.title: pleased not.
entries.content: pleased not. Compare Genesis 26:35 .

entries.title: Mahalath.
entries.content: Mahalath. She had a second name, Bashemath, See Genesis 36:3 .

entries.title: And.
entries.content: And. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ), emphasizing the items in verses: Genesis 28:10-15 .

entries.title: of the stones.
entries.content: of the stones. Hebrew from; i.e. one from among them. Compare verses: Genesis 28:18 , Genesis 28:22 .

entries.title: ladder.
entries.content: ladder. Hebrew. sullam, from salal, to pile up like terraces; a way cast up, stairway. Occurs only here. Compare Isaiah 35:8-10 ; Isaiah 57:14 ; Isaiah 62:10 .

entries.title: the LORD
entries.content:
the LORD = Jehovah.

above it. The Hebrew accent ( zark'a) emphasizes this as meaning "beside him" (Compare Genesis 18:2 , where 'al is rendered "by"). It is not the angels, but the Divine faithfulness and promise, which mark "this place" (verses: Genesis 28:16 , Genesis 28:17 ) and make it "the house of God".

to thee. As He had said to Abraham (Genesis 13:15 ) and to Isaac (Genesis 26:3 ). See note on Genesis 50:24 .

will I. Note the "shalls" and "wills" in this and all these repetitions of Jehovah's covenant.

entries.title: dust . . . &c.
entries.content:
dust . . . &c. Figure of speech Paroemia. App-6 . See on Genesis 15:5 .

in thee. Mark the personal gift, and see note on Genesis 17:7 and Genesis 50:24 .

all. This can be fulfilled only in Christ.

I will not leave thee. This promise first made, here, to Jacob for covenant grace; to the People, for journey (Deuteronomy 31:6 ); to Joshua, for conflict (Joshua 1:5 , Joshua 1:8 ); to Solomon, for work (1 Chronicles 28:20 ); to us, for daily provision (Hebrews 13:5 , Hebrews 13:6 ).

entries.title: Surely.
entries.content:
Surely. Figure of speech Ecphonesis. App-6 .

this place. See on the word "above", Genesis 28:13 .

entries.title: the house of God.
entries.content: the house of God. This "house" is the place where God meets the unworthy in grace. It was so with David (1 Chronicles 22:1 ). It is so for us. Our "place of worship" is where God manifests Himself to us in grace. "The God of all grace" is emphatically "the God of Jacob" (Psalms 146:5 ).

entries.title: the stone.
entries.content:
the stone. See Genesis 28:11 . Not the so-called "Coronation stone" in London: inasmuch as the heads of the "Geological Survey of Great Britain" unanimously declared that "no stone of that kind was to be found in any part of the Holy Land whence it traditionally comes". Prof. Ramsay also pronounced it as being "not known to occur in Egypt or in the rocks around Bethel".

pillar. Afterwards forbidden. Leviticus 26:1 .Deuteronomy 16:22 .

poured oil. A law before Moses. See App-15 .

entries.title: Beth-el.
entries.content: Beth-el. Hebrew the house of El.

entries.title: vowed a vow
entries.content: vowed a vow = made a solemn vow. Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 . The first recorded vow.

entries.title: this stone.
entries.content:
this stone. See verses: Genesis 28:11 , Genesis 28:18 .

God's house. Hebrew. Beth-elohim, not Beth-el.

tenth. See App-15 and Compare Genesis 14:20 .

entries.title: went, &c.
entries.content: went, &c. = lifted up his feet. Hebrew. Idiom, App-6 .

entries.title: well.
entries.content:
well. Hebrew. beer. See note on Genesis 21:19 .

three flocks. Compare Genesis 29:8 .

entries.title: son.
entries.content:
son. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species), put for grandson. Compare Genesis 24:15 . In Genesis 29:12 Jacob calls himself the "brother" of Laban by the same Figure of speech

Lo. Figure of speech Asterismos, App-6 , giving life to the scene.

entries.title: her father's sheep.
entries.content: her father's sheep. Shepherds usually slaves, younger sons, or daughters. Compare David, 1 Samuel 17:13-15 .Exodus 2:16 , Exodus 2:17 . Note exception. Genesis 37:14 , and reason.

entries.title: kissed.
entries.content: kissed. The Eastern greeting.

entries.title: brother.
entries.content: brother. See on Genesis 29:6 and App-29 .

entries.title: heard the tidings.
entries.content: heard the tidings. Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 . "Heard the hearing. "

entries.title: space of a month.
entries.content: space of a month. Hebrew a month of days, i.e., by Figure of speech Hypallage , the days of a month. Compare Numbers 11:20 .

entries.title: Leah.
entries.content:
Leah. Hebrew weary.

Rachel. Hebrew a ewe.

entries.title: tender
entries.content:
tender = weak.

beautiful = comely in form. Compare Genesis 39:6 .

well favoured = comely in countenance.

entries.title: served.
entries.content: served. Compare Hosea 12:12 .

entries.title: Zilpah.
entries.content: Zilpah. See on Genesis 29:29 .

entries.title: behold.
entries.content: behold. Figure of speech Asterismos. To call attention to the fact that he was deceived, as he had deceived Isaac (Genesis 27 ).

entries.title: we,
entries.content: we, i.e. I, by Figure of speech Heterosis (of Number).

entries.title: her
entries.content:
her , i.e. Leah's week.

he gave him Rachel. A popular mistake to suppose that Jacob did not marry Rachel till the end of the second seven years, for in the first seven were born seven sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, and Joseph. In the second seven: Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulon, and Dinah.

entries.title: Bilhah.
entries.content: Bilhah. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Khammurabi, 145. See App-15 .

entries.title: LORD.
entries.content:
LORD. Jehovah used with the five sons (Genesis 29:31-35 and Genesis 30:24 ). Elohim is used with six (Genesis 30:2 , Genesis 30:6 , Genesis 30:17 , Genesis 30:18 , Genesis 30:20 , Genesis 30:23 ). No title used with Benjamin (Genesis 35:16-18 ). All were in pairs. Two pairs from Leah, one pair from Bilhah, one from Zilpah, one from Leah, one from Rachel.

hated. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause), App-6 , by which love and hate are put for the esteem or neglect, caused by love and hate = less loved, Deuteronomy 21:15 .Matthew 6:24 .

entries.title: Reuben.
entries.content:
Reuben. Hebrew. behold a son. For the various orders of the 12 tribes, see App-45 .

heard. Hebrew. sham'a (heard).

Simeon. Hebrew. Shime'on (hearing). Figure of speech Paronomasia.

entries.title: joined.
entries.content:
joined. Hebrew. yillaveh (joined).

Was his name called. Hebrew she called his name, with Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint. Error due to neglected abbreviation in primitive Hebrew text. Figure of speech Paronomasia. App-6 .

Levi. Hebrew. Levi (joiner).

entries.title: praise.
entries.content:
praise. Hebrew. 'odeh (I shall, or. Let me praise) ; ye hudah (he shall be praised). Compare Genesis 49:8 . Figure of speech Paronomasia.

left: i.e. for a time.

entries.title: children.
entries.content: children. Hebrew sons.

entries.title: Bilhah.
entries.content:
Bilhah. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Khammurabi, 145. See App-15 . Compare Genesis 29:29 .

have children. Hebrew be builded up. See note above, and Compare Genesis 16:1-3 .

entries.title: judged.
entries.content:
judged. Hebrew. dananni (judged).

Dan. Hebrew judge. Figure of speech Paronomasia. App-6 .

entries.title: great wrestlings have I wrestled.
entries.content:
great wrestlings have I wrestled. Hebrew with wrestlings of El (= GOD) i.e. mighty wrestlings. Figure of speech Polyptoton, and Paronomasia. App-6 .

Naphtali. Hebrew my wrestling.

entries.title: Zilpah . . . . wife.
entries.content: Zilpah . . . . wife. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Khammurabi, 145. Compare Genesis 16:1-3 ; Genesis 30:3 , Genesis 30:4 . See App-15 .

entries.title: A troop.
entries.content:
A troop. Hebrew over-run, or, have victory; so the Septuagint, Syriac, Arabic, Targum of Onkelos, Vulgate.

Gad = Jupiter (of the Babylonians). See Isaiah 65:11 margin, and Joshua 11:17 ; Joshua 12:7 , where Baal-Gad = the God-Jupiter.

entries.title: Happy.
entries.content:
Happy. Hebrew. be'ashri (happy).

will call, &c. Hebrew. 'ishshruni (sure to call me).

Asher. Hebrew. Asher (happy). Compare Deuteronomy 33:24 . Figure of speech Paronomasia.

entries.title: mandrakes.
entries.content: mandrakes. Septuagint mandragora, the root easily formed, by pinching it, into the shape of a man. Hence its name; also supposed to be and used as a "love-philtre". Arabic = "apples of Satan".

entries.title: hire.
entries.content:
hire. Hebrew. sekari (hire). Figure of speech Paronomasia , with Issachar.

Issachar. Hebrew there is hire, or, he is wages.

entries.title: dowry
entries.content:
dowry = God hath dowered me with a good dowry. Figure of speech Polyptoton.

Zebulun. Hebrew dwelling, or habitation. An Assyrian word, to honour, brought out of Ur.

entries.title: daughter.
entries.content:
daughter. Jacob may have had other daughters not named.

Dinah. Hebrew probably vindication, or, judgment.

entries.title: God remembered.
entries.content:
God remembered. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia. App-6 .

(22-24) Figure of speech Hysterologia, for Joseph born after Naphtali, not after Dinah. This Figure of speech is used to keep Leah's children together.

entries.title: Joseph.
entries.content:
Joseph. Hebrew. yoseph, may He add.

The LORD. Note the occurrence of Jehovah here in connection with Joseph.

shall add. Hebrew. yoseph, is adding. Figure of speech Paronomasia, App-6 .

entries.title: tarry:
entries.content:
tarry: for. Figure of speech Ellipsis, which requires some such supply.

experience = by divination. Heb, nihashti, from nahash (Genesis 3:1 ).

entries.title: provide.
entries.content:
provide. Hebrew the verb to do, which by Metonymy (of the Cause), means to provide, or, do for.

house. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject), App-6 , by which "house "is put for all who dwell in it.

entries.title: answer.
entries.content:
answer. By the Figure of speech Prosopopoeia, righteousness is personified.

in time to come. Hebrew. to-morrow. Figure of speech Antimereia (of Adverb), App-6 = some future day.

entries.title: the man
entries.content:
the man . Hebrew. ha- 'ish . App-14 .

exceedingly . Hebrew. meod meod = greatly greatly. Figure of speech Epizeuxis. App-6

entries.title: glory.
entries.content: glory. Hebrew weight. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Effect), App-6 = wealth, the effect (i.e. the burden or weight) being put for that which caused it.

entries.title: as before.
entries.content: as before. Hebrew yesterday and the day before. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Part), = aforetime.

entries.title: your father:
entries.content: your father: repeated at beginning of next verse by the Figure of speech Anadiplosis.

entries.title: suffered him not.
entries.content:
suffered him not. Figure of speech Idioma. Hebrew did not give him to do me evil.

hurt. Hebrew. ra'a' . See App-44 .

entries.title: angel of God
entries.content: angel of God (Hebrew. Elohim). In Genesis 31:13 called by Himself, "I am the God of Beth-el", El of Beth-el. Compare Genesis 28:12 , Genesis 28:13 , and Genesis 48:16 .

entries.title: cattle.
entries.content: cattle. Compare Psalms 50:10 .

entries.title: vowedst a vow.
entries.content: vowedst a vow. Figure of speech Polyptoton, App-6 = madest a solemn vow.

entries.title: Is there yet, &c. ?
entries.content: Is there yet, &c. ? Figure of speech Erotesis.

entries.title: images.
entries.content: images. Hebrew. teraphim, a kind of household gods, showing that the idolatry of Babylonia still clung to Laban's family, in spite of his protestations in Genesis 31:20 ; Genesis 30:27 . Compare Genesis 31:30 ; Genesis 35:2 .

entries.title: unawares to Laban.
entries.content: unawares to Laban. Hebrew stole the heart. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Part), App-6 , heart being put for knowledge. Compare Genesis 31:27 . Rachel stole Laban's idols; and Jacob stole Laban's heart.

entries.title: the river
entries.content:
the river = the Euphrates. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Genus).

Gilead = perpetual fountain. Compare Numbers 32:1 , Numbers 32:39 . Deuteronomy 3:12-16 ; Deuteronomy 34:1 .

entries.title: brethren.
entries.content: brethren. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species), App-6 , one relationship put for a general one.

entries.title: good or bad.
entries.content: good or bad. Hebrew from good to bad.

entries.title: with mirth.
entries.content: with mirth. Laban adds hypocrisy, covetousness, and avarice, to idolatry.

entries.title: sons.
entries.content: sons. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Species), sons put for grandsons, &c.

entries.title: hand.
entries.content:
hand. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Part), hand put for the whole person, "in my power".

you and your are plural. God of your father. In Genesis 30:27 , Genesis 30:30 , Laban had spoken of the LORD = Jehovah; now he has sunk so low as to say' your" God, and calls the teraphim "my gods".

entries.title: sore longedst.
entries.content:
sore longedst. Hebrew with longing thou hast longed. Figure of speech Polyptoton.

my gods. Compare on Genesis 31:29 .

entries.title: let him not live.
entries.content: let him not live. This was in strict accordance with the Code of Khammurabi (9), but in contrast with the Mosaic law. See App-15 .

entries.title: Rachel.
entries.content:
Rachel. Repeated by the Figure of speech Anadiplosis. Hebrew "tent of Rachel, and Rachel had taken. "

furniture = saddle.

searched = felt [with his hands].

entries.title: Rachel.
entries.content:
Rachel. Repeated by the Figure of speech Anadiplosis. Hebrew "tent of Rachel, and Rachel had taken. "

furniture = saddle.

searched = felt [with his hands].

entries.title: my lord.
entries.content:
my lord. Hebrew the eyes of my lord. Figure of speech Prosopopoeia. App-6 .

custom. Laban's deceit begets deceit.

entries.title: twenty.
entries.content: twenty. The No. of disappointed expectancy. See App-10 .

entries.title: my hand.
entries.content: my hand. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Part), hand put for "me". Compare Genesis 31:29 .

entries.title: Thus I was.
entries.content:
Thus I was. Figure of speech Ellipsis = "Thus (wherever) I was".

droughts heat. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Effect), effect put for the burning heat which caused it. Contrast with cold produced by the frost.

my sleep. The Eastern shepherd often away from home for weeks at a time.

entries.title: the fear.
entries.content:
the fear. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct). App-6 , fear put for the God Whom Jacob worshipped.

with me = on my side. Psalms 118:6 , Psalms 118:7 .

entries.title: make.
entries.content: make. Hebrew cut (Compare Genesis 15:10 , Genesis 15:18 ) = solemnize.

entries.title: pillar.
entries.content: pillar. Compare Genesis 28:18 .

entries.title: eat:
entries.content: eat: i.e. of the covenant sacrifices. Compare Genesis 26:30 . Exodus 24:5 , Exodus 24:11 .

entries.title: Jegar-sahadutha.
entries.content: Jegar-sahadutha. Chaldaic = witness-heap.

entries.title: Mizpah.
entries.content:
Mizpah. Hebrew watch-tower.

he. i.e. Laban. So that he knew Hebrew as well as Chaldee.

the LORD. Laban also uses the name Jehovah. It is used by all the speakers in Genitive except the Nachash (Genesis 3 ), Abimelech (when speaking to Abram, not to Isaac), the sons of Heth, Pharaoh, Joseph's brethren, and Joseph himself.

absent. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), App-6 = Hebrew hidden, put for absent.

entries.title: pillar.
entries.content: pillar. Distinct from the "heap". Compare Genesis 31:45 , Genesis 31:46 .

entries.title: offered sacrifice
entries.content: offered sacrifice = killed beasts. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct).

entries.title: sons.
entries.content:
sons. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Part). Put for grandsons as well.

daughters . Also for granddaughters. The second vision, corresponding with that of Bethel: See Genesis 28:10-22 .

entries.title: angels of God.
entries.content: angels of God. Compare Psalms 34:7 , to assure him of God's presence with him, and of His protection.

entries.title: host
entries.content:
host = camp. Hebrew. mahaneh as in verses: Genesis 32:8 , Genesis 32:21 . Compare Deuteronomy 33:2 .Joshua 5:14 , Joshua 5:15 .Psalms 27:3 ; Psalms 78:28 ; Psalms 106:16 .

Mahanaim = two camps.

entries.title: and.
entries.content:
In Genesis 32:7-12 and Genesis 32:13-32 note that Jacob alternately uses means as though there were no such thing as prayer; and then prays as though there were no such things as means. We may use means, but not trust in them.

and. The Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ) shows the care with which he prepared.

two bands = two camps. Same word (and perhaps idea) as in Genesis 32:2 .

entries.title: saidst.
entries.content:
Jacob's first prayer acknowledges both Elohim and Jehovah.

saidst. Compare Genesis 32:12 with Genesis 31:13 .

entries.title: I am not worthy.
entries.content:
I am not worthy. Hebrew I have proved unworthy. Figure of speech Heterosis (of Tense), App-6 . = I have been and am unworthy.

mercies. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). First occurance of plural

my staff. Having nothing and deserving nothing but chastisement. Hence, the God who met him there (the God of Bethel) is "the God of Jacob", and is "the God of all grace" (1 Peter 5:10 ): compare Psalms 146:5 .

entries.title: with.
entries.content: with. Hebrew upon. As though sons slain first and mothers falling on them.

entries.title: saidst.
entries.content:
saidst. Compare Genesis 32:9 with Genesis 28:13-15 .

as the sand. Figure of speech Paroemia. See note on Genesis 13:16 .

entries.title: present.
entries.content: present. See App-43 .

entries.title: will appease him.
entries.content:
will appease him. Hebrew "cover his face", i.e. hide my offence from him: "face" being put by Synecdoche (of the Part), for himself.

of me. Hebrew my face. Synecdoche (of the Part), App-6 .

entries.title: Jabbok.
entries.content: Jabbok. Hebrew pouring out, or emptying.

entries.title: a Man.
entries.content:
a Man. Hebrew. 'ish. App-14 . Called "God" (verses: Genesis 32:28 , Genesis 32:30 ), an "Angel", and Jehovah Elohim, Hosea 12:4 , Hosea 12:5 .

breaking. Hebrew going up. Figure of speech Antimereia (of Verb Part, for noun).

entries.title: day breaketh.
entries.content: day breaketh. Hebrew dawn hath ascended.

entries.title: What is thy name?
entries.content: What is thy name? Figure of speech Anthropopatheia. For He knew his name.

entries.title: Jacob
entries.content:
Jacob = contender (Genesis 25:22 ). Used of the natural Jacob and his natural seed. Israel used for spiritual Jacob and his spiritual seed.

Israel = "God commands, orders or rules". Man attempts it but always, in the end, fails. Out of some forty Hebrew names compounded with "El" or "Jah", God is always the doer of what the verb means (compare Dani-el, God judges).

prince = commander, orderer. Here used not to dignify but to reproach. Compare Genesis 12:15 , princes (courtiers); Genesis 26:26 , chief of soldiers; Genesis 39:1 , officer; Genesis 40:2 , chief; Genesis 40:3 , jailor; Genesis 47:6 , herdsmen; Exodus 1:11 , taskmasters, &c.

hast thou power = hast thou contended. Jacob had contended with Esau in the womb, and thus got his name Jacob, which is referred to here in reproach, not in eulogy.

prevailed = succeeded. He had contended for the birthright and succeeded (Genesis 25:29-34 ). He had contended for the blessing and succeeded (27). He had contended with Laban and succeeded (31). He had contended with "men" and succeeded. Now he contends with God and fails. Hence his name was changed to Isra-el, God commands, to teach him the greatly needed lesson of dependence upon God.

entries.title: Peniel
entries.content:
Peniel = Hebrew God's face.

seen. Compare Genesis 16:13 .

life = soul. Hebrew. nephesh. See App-13 .

entries.title: he.
entries.content:
he. Emph. to call attention to the fact that he was not only late, but limping.

halted = limped. The sign that it is God who commands, and has real power to overcome. Typical of the national humiliation required before entering on the blessing.

entries.title: sinew
entries.content: sinew = the ligament of the hip joint.

entries.title: men
entries.content: men = Hebrew sing, 'ish ( App-14 ), as we use the expression "400 foot". When plural, used only of angels.

entries.title: and kissed him.
entries.content: and kissed him. This is one of the Hebrew words with "extraordinary points", to show that the Massorites thought it should be omitted. See App-31 . It should read, "and fell on his neck and wept"; without kissing. This is the custom in Genesis. Compare Genesis 45:14 ; Genesis 46:29 .

entries.title: enough
entries.content: enough = abundance, plenty.

entries.title: Jacob said.
entries.content: Jacob said. Figure of speech Ellipsis . ( App-6 ). Ellipsis should be supplied thus: "Jacob [refused, and] said. "

entries.title: men.
entries.content: men. Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint read "I".

entries.title: What needeth it?
entries.content: What needeth it? Hebrew What for? or Why so? Figure of speech Erotesis and Ellipsis ( App-6 )= Why [have] anything?

entries.title: booths.
entries.content: booths. Hebrew. succoth. Hence the name. First occurance.

entries.title: came to Shalem,
entries.content: came to Shalem, a city of Shechem; read, came in peace to the city of Shechem; the Hebrew Shalem means peace.

entries.title: Hamor.
entries.content: Hamor. Probably a title, like Abimelech and Pharaoh.

entries.title: El-elohe-Israel -
entries.content: El-elohe-Israel - "GOD-the God-of-Israel", but not the place for this altar. Compare Genesis 35:1 .

entries.title: daughter of Leah.
entries.content: daughter of Leah. Compare Genesis 30:21 , and own sister of Simeon and Lev 29:33 , Lev 29:34 .

entries.title: defiled.
entries.content: defiled. Hebrew humbled.

entries.title: his soul
entries.content:
his soul = himself. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Part). App-6 , Hebrew. nephesh.

kindly. Hebrew on her heart (as though making an impression on it).

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content: Israel. The first Occurance in a collective sense.

entries.title: soul.
entries.content: soul. Hebrew. nephesh . App-13 . Figure of speech. Synecdoche (of Part) and Pleonasm, ( App-6 ), to emphasise the intensity of the longing.

entries.title: gift.
entries.content: gift. The noun put by Metonymy for the verb = ask me to give, &c.

entries.title: deceitfully.
entries.content: deceitfully. Jacob ' s character his own scourge. The first and only occurance in Genesis.

entries.title: behold.
entries.content: behold. Figure of speech. Asterismos . App-6 .

entries.title: Shall not, &c.
entries.content: Shall not, &c. Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 .

entries.title: man.
entries.content: man. Heb. 'ish . See App-14 .

entries.title: edge.
entries.content: edge. Hebrew mouth. Figure of speech Pleonasm . The acts of Jacob and his sons at Shechem may be contrasted with those of Abraham (Genesis 12:6 ), and of Joshua (Joshua 24:1-27 ), and of Christ (John 4:5 ).

entries.title: The sons.
entries.content: The sons. Some MSS. read "And the sons".

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Note the Figure of speech. Polysyndeton , App-6 . to emphasise each item, in Genesis 34:28-29 .

entries.title: wealth.
entries.content: wealth. Hebrew strength. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct). Strength put for the wealth which it acquires.

entries.title: Canaanites.
entries.content: Canaanites. Descendants of the Nephilim. See Genesis 12:6 and App-23 and App-25 .

entries.title: Should he ... ?
entries.content: Should he ... ? Figure of speech. Erotesis . App-6 .

entries.title: God.
entries.content:
God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

Jacob. See notes on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

Beth-el. House of GOD. Hebrew. El. App-4 (Genesis 28:19 ).

entries.title: Put away.
entries.content:
Put away. Purification necessary in going up to Beth-el = the house of God.

strange gods. Doubtless part of the spoils taken from the houses of the Shechemites. Compare Genesis 35:4 , and See Genesis 34:28 , Genesis 34:29 .

be clean. First occurance. Here and always used of ceremonial cleansing

entries.title: with me.
entries.content: with me. Compare Genesis 28:20 ; Genesis 3:3 ; Gen 3:42 .

entries.title: Jacob
entries.content:
Jacob = Supplanter, or Contender. See on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

earrings. Showing that the "strange gods" were part of the booty: probably of precious metals.

entries.title: God.
entries.content: God. Hebrew. Elohim . App-4 .

entries.title: Luz.
entries.content: Luz. Compare Genesis 28:19 .

entries.title: El-Beth-el
entries.content:
El-Beth-el = GOD of the House of GOD.

appeared: or revealed Himself.

his brother. Some Manuscripts, with Samaritan Pentateuch, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, Syriac, read "Esau his brother".

entries.title: Deborah Rebekah's nurse.
entries.content:
Deborah Rebekah's nurse. We hear no more of Rebekah from the time Jacob left home (Genesis 27:45 ), not even of her death! Deborah may have come with a message, or she may, on Rebekah's death, have joined his household.

Allon-bachuth. Hebrew The oak of weeping.

entries.title: Israel
entries.content: Israel = GOD rules. See note on Genesis 32:28 .

entries.title: GOD ALMIGHTY
entries.content: GOD ALMIGHTY = Hebrew. El-Shaddai, GOD the all-bountiful or allsufficient. The title which best accords with the promise here given.

entries.title: I gave.
entries.content: I gave. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). App-6 . = which I promised to give.

entries.title: He.
entries.content: He. i.e. God.

entries.title: set up a pillar
entries.content:
set up a pillar = Hebrew pillared a pillar. Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 .

poured a drink offering. See App-15 . First occurrence of "drink offering": afterward provided for in Leviticus 23:13 , Leviticus 23:18 , Leviticus 23:37 , and in Numbers 15:5-10 . Always "poured out, "never drunk.

entries.title: Ephrath.
entries.content: Ephrath. Hebrew fertility.

entries.title: her soul
entries.content:
her soul = her life. Hebrew. nephesh ( App-13 ), rendered "life" in Genesis 1:20 .

in departing = ebbing away, or failing (Genesis 42:28 . Song of Solomon 5:6 ); or ending (Exodus 23:16 ). In Ezekiel 7:10 rendered "gone forth"; Exodus 23:26 . In Ezekiel 26:18 rendered "departure".

Ben-oni = Son of my sorrow.

Benjamin = Son of my right hand. The word rendered "sorrow" ( 'avon ) is a Homonym, the other meaning being "strength", and is so rendered in Genesis 49:3 .Deuteronomy 21:17 . Job 18:7 , Job 18:12 &c. It is rendered "mourning" in Deuteronomy 26:14 .Hosea 9:4 . This Homonym is the basis of Jacobs change of Benjamin's name. The Authorized Version and Revised Version both recognize this Homonym.

entries.title: Beth-lehem
entries.content: Beth-lehem = House of bread.

entries.title: grave.
entries.content:
grave. Hebrew. keber, first Occurance. Genesis 23:4 . = A sepulchre, from kabar to bury. Not sheol, which = THE grave. Compare App-35 .

unto this day. Wellknown in the days of Samuel. See 1 Samuel 10:2 .

entries.title: lay with.
entries.content:
lay with. Compare Genesis 49:4 .

twelve. The number of governmental perfection. See App-10 . Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Whole), App-6 . For the various orders of the twelve tribes, see App-45 ,

entries.title: came.
entries.content: came. It does not follow that Jacob did not often see Isaac. As soon as Isaac was married, Abraham disappears from the history. It is the same with Isaac when Jacob married: and the same with Jacob when Joseph comes into prominence. They do not appear together in the history: but Abraham is described as "dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob " (Hebrews 11:9 ).

entries.title: and died.
entries.content:
and died. Figure of speech Synonymia, for great emphasis. They all mean the same thing, repeated in other words, to add solemnity to the event.

was gathered. See note on Genesis 49:33 . 2 Samuel 12:23 .

entries.title: generations.
entries.content: generations. Given here, as no more is to be said about him.

entries.title: Adah.
entries.content:
Adah. Her second name was Bashemath, Genesis 26:34 .

Aholibamah. Her second name was Genesis 26:34 ; and her father, Anah, got a second name also from his discovery of the hot springs (see note on "rnules", Genesis 36:24 ). in Genesis 26:34 , called Hittite, because Hittite included Hivite.

daughter. Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Syriac read "son".

entries.title: Bashemath
entries.content: Bashemath also had a second name, Mahalath, Genesis 28:9 .

entries.title: and.
entries.content:
and. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton, App-6 , pointing with emphasis to each item.

persons = souls, Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

Canaan. Esau's sons, born in the land wen t out of it. Jacob's sons, all born out of it and went into it.

Jacob. "Unto Seir" should be added, according to Ginsburg Hebrew Text.

entries.title: Esau is Edom.
entries.content: Esau is Edom. Should be "Esau, he is Edom".

entries.title: Teman.
