entries.content: Teman. Whence came Eliphaz the Temanite. Job 2:11 ; Job 15:1 .

entries.title: Amalek.
entries.content:
Amalek. One of Israel's bitterest foes, with whom Jehovah has perpetual war, Exodus 17:8 , Exodus 17:14 . Compare Numbers 24:20 . Deuteronomy 25:17-19 . The land of A. so-called by Figure of speech Prolepsis ( App-6 .), in Genesis 14:7 .

sons. The "sons" of Adah are her son and grandsons.

entries.title: dukes.
entries.content: dukes. Hebrew chiefs, or, chieftains.

entries.title: who inhabited, &c.
entries.content: who inhabited, &c. The Horites were a branch of the Nephilim. See App-23 and App-25 .

entries.title: children
entries.content:
children = sons.

Timna. Compare Genesis 36:12 .

entries.title: both.
entries.content:
both. Some codices, with Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Syriac, omit "both".

found. Heb, matza, to happen on, discover (not invent); to find (not find out).

m ul

es. Hab. hayyemim, hot springs (with Vulgate and Syriac), hence Anah got the name of Beeri from Beer, a well, Compare Genesis 26:34 ; and to distinguish him from the Anah of Genesis 36:20 .

entries.title: before there reigned.
entries.content: before there reigned. The reference is to Genesis 17:6 and Genesis 35:11 .Deuteronomy 17:14-20 .

entries.title: the river,
entries.content: the river, i.e. the Euphrates.

entries.title: The whole chapter,
entries.content:
The whole chapter, Figure of speech Hysterologia. App-6 . The last of the eleven Toledoth

Jacob. See notes on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

Wherein = of his father ' s sojournings. S Bilhah. i.e. Dan and Naphtali, Genesis 30:6-8 .

Zilpah. i.e. Gad and Asher, Genesis 30:10-13 .

his. Hebrew their.

entries.title: coat:
entries.content:
coat: with long sleeves, worn only by the chief and his heir. This the first cause of brothers' enmity. See note on Genesis 27:15 with Genesis 25:31 .

colours. Not "pieces". Marking it as priestly or royal. Exodus 28:4 , Exodus 28:39 ; Exodus 39:1 . 2Sa 13:18 , 2 Samuel 13:19 . Psalms 45:14 .

entries.title: brethren.
entries.content: brethren. Hebrew sons.

entries.title: dreamed a dream.
entries.content: dreamed a dream. Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 . For emphasis = had a significant dream.

entries.title: in the field
entries.content:
in the field = in the midst of the field.

stood upright. Hebrew took its stand, or was set upright.

entries.title: shalt thou, &c.
entries.content: shalt thou, &c. Figure of speech Erotesis. Compare the rejection of Moses, Exodus 2:14 ; and of Christ, Luke 19:14 .

entries.title: eleven stars
entries.content:
eleven stars = the eleven signs of the Zodiac, Joseph being the twelfth. See note on Numbers 2:2 .

made obeisance. Compare Genesis 42:6 ; Genesis 43:26 ; Genesis 44:14 .

entries.title: their father's flock.
entries.content: their father's flock. One of the fifteen expressions with the extraordinary points (see App-31 ), indicating a doubtful reading, and suggesting that they had gone to feed themselves and make merry.

entries.title: the flock.
entries.content:
the flock. With the omission in Genesis 37:12 these words are unnecessary.

Shechem. Was Jacob afraid after Genesis 34:25-30 ?

entries.title: Dothan.
entries.content: Dothan. On the high road to Egypt for caravans from the East.

entries.title: conspired.
entries.content: conspired. Compare Matthew 27:1 .

entries.title: dreamer.
entries.content: dreamer. Hebrew master (or lord, Baal) of dreams.

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ), emphasizing the deliberateness of their actions.

entries.title: him
entries.content: him = his soul. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

entries.title: that he might rid him, &c.
entries.content: that he might rid him, &c. Figure of speech Parenthesis , by way of explanation.

entries.title: his coat.
entries.content: his coat. See on Genesis 37:3 .

entries.title: sat down.
entries.content:
sat down. Showing their indifference. Compare Genesis 42:21 and Matthew 27:36 .

company = caravan. There was a wellorganized trade in sixteenth dynasty.

Ishmeelites. Son 39:1 . In Genesis 37:28 and Genesis 37:36 called Midianites. Ishmael was the son of Abraham by Hagar (Genesis 16:11 , Genesis 16:12 ); Midian the son of Abraham by Keturah (Genesis 25:2 ). See Judges 8:24 , Judges 8:25 , where they were mixed together, and were distinguished only by their noserings. (Compare Genesis 24:47 ; Genesis 35:4 .Exodus 32:2 , &c.)

entries.title: sell him.
entries.content:
sell him. A Judas sold Joseph, and a Judas sold Christ. Slaves were in great demand in Egypt.

were content = hearkened.

entries.title: Midianites.
entries.content:
Midianites. See note on Genesis 37:25 .

they, i.e. Joseph's brethren.

twenty. The number of disappointed expectancy. See App-10 .

entries.title: whither.
entries.content:
whither. Figure of speech Erotesis.

go = go in, as though to hide himself

entries.title: killed.
entries.content: killed. Heb, shahath. See App-42 .

entries.title: And.
entries.content:
And. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ), in verses: Genesis 37:33 , Genesis 37:34 , to emphasize the successive steps in Jacob's grief.

without doubt. Figure of speech Polyptoton , "tearing he has been torn". Deceived by the blood of a kid, as he had deceived his father with the skin of a kid, Genesis 27:16 .

entries.title: all his daughters.
entries.content:
all his daughters. See on Genesis 30:21 , or it may be Synecdoche (of the Part), App-6 , put for all his female relatives and granddaughters.

grave. Hebrew. Sheol, first occurance of word. See App-35 .

entries.title: Potiphar
entries.content:
Potiphar = consecrated to Ra : one of the gods of lower Egypt.

captain of the guard. Compare 2 Kings 25:8 , 2 Kings 25:11 , 2 Kings 25:20 had charge of police, as well as military duties. The whole Chapter is the Figure of speech Parecbasis ( App-6 ).

entries.title: certain, &c.
entries.content: certain, &c. = a man, an Adullamite. Hebrew. 'ish. See App-14 .

entries.title: Canaanite.
entries.content: Canaanite. In this was Judah's sin. Compare Genesis 24:3 ; Genesis 26:35 ; Genesis 27:46 ; Genesis 28:1 .Exodus 34:16 . Deuteronomy 7:3 . A warning, and a revelation of the human heart. Note who these Canaanites were! App-23 .

entries.title: he,
entries.content: he, should be "she", with Septuagint.

entries.title: raise up seed, &c.
entries.content: raise up seed, &c. = a law before Sinai. See App-15 . Compare Deuteronomy 25:5-9 . Ruth 4:10 . Matthew 22:24 . An old and present Eastern law.

entries.title: displeased.
entries.content: displeased. Hebrew was evil in the eyes of Jehovah. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia. App-6 .

entries.title: he die also.
entries.content: he die also. Judah, an unnatural brother, is punished in his own children.

entries.title: And
entries.content:
And Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ) emphasizing the deliberateness of each action.

in an open place. Hebrew "in the entrance to Enaim".

entries.title: widowhood.
entries.content: widowhood. Nine widows mentioned. See App-10 for significance. Tamar, here. Tekoah, 2 Samuel 14:5 . Hiram's mother, 1 Kings 7:14 . Zeruah, 1 Kings 11:26 . Widow of Zarephath, 1 Kings 17:9 . Poor widow, Mark 12:42 . Anna, Luke 2:37 . Widow of Nain, Luke 7:12 . Importunate, Luke 18:3 .

entries.title: openly.
entries.content: openly. Hebrew "at Enaim".

entries.title: burnt.
entries.content: burnt. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Hammurabi (157), which was then in force throughout Canaan. See App-15 .

entries.title: Pharez
entries.content: Pharez = "breach".

entries.title: Zarah
entries.content: Zarah = "a rising of light", "Offspring", or "Dawn". Both Pharez and Zarah, together with their rnother Tamar, are in the genealogy of Christ (Matthew 1:3 ). This is why this parenthetical chapter is inserted here. It is here by the Figure of speech Parecbasis . It comes, historically, before chapter 37.

entries.title: Potiphar.
entries.content:
Potiphar. See note on Genesis 37:36 .

guard = executioners.

Egyptian. This is emphasized three times (verses: Genesis 39:1 , Genesis 39:2 , Genesis 39:5 ); because recent discoveries show that Egypt was at this time under a new dynasty; and emphasis is put on the fact that Potiphar, though an "Egyptian", was retained in high position.

Ishmeelites. See note on chapter Genesis 37:25 .

entries.title: was
entries.content: was = = it came to be. See Genesis 1:2 .

entries.title: served
entries.content:
served = became his personal servant.

hand. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). App-6 . Hand put for care which it takes.

entries.title: in the house, &c.
entries.content: in the house, &c. = at home or abroad.

entries.title: he
entries.content:
he = Potiphar. Figure of speech Ellipsis.

left. Hebrew. 'azab, a Homonym. Its other meaning is "to help". See note on Exodus 23:5 .

knew. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). App-6 . Knowing put for caring for.

bread. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species). Bread put for all kinds of food.

eat. He knew and cared for that, as the Egyptians might not eat with Hebrews (Genesis 43:32 ).

goodly, &c. Exactly what is said of his mother, Genesis 29:17 .

entries.title: wife.
entries.content: wife. Egyptian women were not secluded as the Syrian women were. This is shown by the Egyptian paintings of the period.

entries.title: he refused.
entries.content:
he refused. Joseph (now reckoned the first-born, 1 Chronicles 5:2 ): thus by his chastity shames the unchastity of Reuben the first-born before.

wotteth not = knoweth not. Old English. Idiom.

entries.title: wickedness.
entries.content:
wickedness. Heb r'a'a. See App-44 .

sin. Heh. chat'a. .

entries.title: went into the house.
entries.content: went into the house. Pictures of an Egyptian house are extant which show the store-room at the back of the house.

entries.title: garment.
entries.content: garment. Hebrew. beged. Compare Genesis 37:31 , Genesis 37:32 . That, to cover the sin of his brethren; this, to cover the sin of Potiphar's wife.

entries.title: See.
entries.content: See. Figure of speech Asterismos. App-6 .

entries.title: After this manner
entries.content: After this manner = According to these words.

entries.title: prison
entries.content: prison = the house of the fortress.

entries.title: mercy
entries.content: mercy = kindness.

entries.title: keepers
entries.content: keepers = governor,

entries.title: butler
entries.content:
butler = the cupbearer. Nehemiah 1:11 .

baker. A Papyrus, in the National Library, Paris (nineteenth dynasty), gives the name of a similar officer (Djadja), the chief; and mentions "114,064 loaves made in the white fortress". (See Records of the Past, vol. ii, p. 126.)

entries.title: season.
entries.content: season. Hebrew days (Genesis 4:3 ) = either "some days" (Genesis 4:3 ), or, perhaps, a year.

entries.title: dreamed a dream.
entries.content: dreamed a dream. Figure of speech Polyptoton ( App-6 ), i.e. had a significant or important dream.

entries.title: pressed, &c.
entries.content: pressed, &c. A religious ceremony, connected with the worship of Horus, portrayed in Egyptian paintings. Existence of vines in Egypt has been denied by critics; but now they are seen depicted in paintings. In the cup was honey, or some other liquid, with which the grape juice was mixed.

entries.title: are.
entries.content: are. Should be "they [are]".

entries.title: lift up thine head
entries.content: lift up thine head = uplift thee, i.e. restore thee to favour. For this was the highest honour that the cupbearer could have.

entries.title: think on me, &c.
entries.content: think on me, &c. Compare Luke 23:42 .

entries.title: white,
entries.content: white, or, wicker.

entries.title: are
entries.content: are = "they [are]. "

entries.title: from off thee.
entries.content: from off thee. Contrast this with Genesis 40:13 .

entries.title: birthday.
entries.content: birthday. These were observed with great ceremony and state. Critics have supposed it to be only a Persian custom. The Rosetta stone contains a decree concerning the keeping of the birthday feast of Ptolemy Epiphanes.

entries.title: restored.
entries.content: restored. Compare Genesis 40:13 , and See Genesis 41:1 , Genesis 41:3 .

entries.title: hanged.
entries.content:
hanged. Compare Genesis 40:19 , and See Genesis 41:13 .

as = according as.

entries.title: but forgat him.
entries.content: but forgat him. Figure of speech Pleonasm. App-6 . Used for great emphasis. Compare Amos 6:6 .

entries.title: the river:
entries.content: the river: i e. the Nile.

entries.title: seven . . . kine.
entries.content:
seven . . . kine. The cow was the emblem of Isis. In the Egyptian "Book of the Dead", Osiris is represented as a bull, accompanied by seven cows. (British Museum.) This was the basis of the dream, and gave it such significance and mystery.

in a meadow = among the rushes, or reeds, ' ahu , probably an Egyptian word.

entries.title: seven ears.
entries.content:
seven ears. Unknown to us; but common in Egypt with the Triticum composition.

rank = fat.

entries.title: east wind.
entries.content: east wind. In Egypt the prevailing winds are N. and S.: in Palestine E. and W. The wind here is the Ckamsin (Hebrew. kadim), which is southeast, and is a blighting wind. Hebrews had only the four quarters. Had it said here south, it would have meant nothing, but east conveys the nature of the wind, especially as evil was supposed to come from the east and good from the west, as in other countries.

entries.title: spirit.
entries.content:
spirit. Hebrew. ruach. See App-9 .

magicians. Priests were divided into four classes; and five priests chosen from them were the king's councillors.

entries.title: remember
entries.content: remember = bring to [Pharaoh's] remembrance.

entries.title: as
entries.content:
as = according as.

he restored: he = Joseph. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). i.e. he declared I should be restored.

he hanged: he = Joseph. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). App-6 . = declared he would be hanged.

entries.title: brought him hastily out.
entries.content:
brought him hastily out. Hebrew made him run.

shaved. The beard was a disgrace in Egypt; shaving a disgrace in Palestine. Compare 1 Samuel 10:4 .

entries.title: dreamed a dream.
entries.content: dreamed a dream. Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 . = I have had a significant dream.

entries.title: the river
entries.content: the river = the Nile.

entries.title: is.
entries.content: is. Heb, "it [is]".

entries.title: are.
entries.content: are. Hebrew "they [are]".

entries.title: seven years.
entries.content:
seven years. This explains and confirms the hieroglyphic inscription discovered by Wilbour at Sehel (first cataract). It is referred to in another inscription in the tomb of Baba, at El-Kab, translated by Brugsch (History of Egypt, i, 304). In July 1908, Brugsch Bey discovered inscriptions which tell how "for seven successive years the Nile did not overflow, and vegetation withered and failed; that the land was devoid of crops, and that during these years, famine and misery devastated the land of Egypt". The date is given as 1700 B. C, which cannot be earlier, therefore, than the last year of the famine. The last year of the seven years of plenty was in B.C. 1708, according to Ussher (Genesis 41:53 ), with which the inscription agrees. See farther, App-37 .

the land. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). App-6 . the people in the land.

entries.title: doubled.
entries.content:
doubled. To denote its establishment by God. Compare Isaiah 40:2 ; Isaiah 61:7 . Jeremiah 16:18 ; Jeremiah 17:18 . Zechariah 9:12 .Revelation 18:6 .

twice. Figure of speech Ellipsis ( App-6 ) = "[and sent] twice. "

entries.title: do this
entries.content: do this = take action.

entries.title: the spirit.
entries.content: the spirit. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 . No art. = a Divine spirit or inspiration. Pharaoh knew nothing of Biblical Psychology.

entries.title: word.
entries.content:
word. Hebrew mouth. Metonymy (of Cause). Mouth is put for the commands uttered by it.

be ruled. Hebrew. nashak, to bend (as a bow). Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct). = bend put for submit. See Genesis 41:43 , below, "Bow the knee", and note on "kiss", Psalms 2:12 .

greater. Compare Genesis 45:8 .

entries.title: all.
entries.content: all. Apepi only recently ruled over all. Before this he had reigned with his father and grandfather. So the Monuments.

entries.title: they.
entries.content:
they. Some codices, with Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Syriac, read "one".

Bow the knee. This is not Hebrew "tender father", as Authorized Version margin, but Egyptian. Abrek = bend or bow the knee. See Genesis 41:40 above, and Psalms 2:12 . Compare Genesis 45:8 , and John 8:8 in Coptic NT. ("stooped down"). A command still used in Egypt to make camels kneel (" Abrok "). According to Sayce, Abrek is a Sumerian title = -"The Seer". This would demand prostration.

entries.title: Zaphnath-paaneah.
entries.content:
Zaphnath-paaneah. This, too, is not Hebrew, but Egyptian. Zap = abundance; nt ( nath ) = of ; pa = the; aneh = life. The whole name = abundance of life, or, of food for the living.

Poti-pherah. The Egyptian priest of On = "City of the Sun", called in Hebrew. Aven and Bethshemesh (Jeremiah 43:13 ), and in Greek. Heliopolis. It was the university of Old Egypt.

entries.title: all the food.
entries.content:
all the food. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Whole), food put for corn.

Which were. Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint read "in which there was plenty".

entries.title: sand, &c.
entries.content: sand, &c. Figure of speech Paroemia ( App-6 ).

entries.title: name.
entries.content:
name. Figure of speech Pleonasm.

toil. Heb, 'amal. App-44 .

entries.title: was
entries.content: was = came to pass. See note on Genesis 1:2 .

entries.title: dearth.
entries.content:
dearth. One of 13 famines. See note on Genesis 12:10 . Gen 12:57

all countries. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). i.e. people from all countries.

all lands. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of the Whole). i.e. all neighbouring lands,

entries.title: Why . . . ? &c.
entries.content: Why . . . ? &c. Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 . That is what we all too often do when in trouble or difficulty.

entries.title: and not die.
entries.content: and not die. Figure of speech Pleonasm. for emphasis.

entries.title: in Egypt.
entries.content: in Egypt. Some Codices read "from the Egyptians".

entries.title: was.
entries.content:
was. Hebrew "he [was]".

bowed down. Compare Genesis 37:7 , Genesis 37:8 .

entries.title: roughly.
entries.content: roughly. Each step in Joseph's treatment must be noted, all tending to one end: viz.: to bring them back to the pit at Dothan, convict them of their sin, and compel their confession of it. That climax is not reached till verse Genesis 42:21 . Judah's words voice it, Genesis 44:18-34 .

entries.title: remembered.
entries.content:
remembered. Compare Genesis 37:5 , Genesis 37:9 .

nakedness. Figure of speech Prosopopoeia. App-6 .

entries.title: We are, &c.
entries.content: We are, &c. Hebrew "all of us the sons of one man [are] we".

entries.title: the sons.
entries.content: the sons. Heb "we [are]". See note on Genesis 42:11 .

entries.title: proved.
entries.content: proved. Joseph, from his high position, could make very strict inquiry.

entries.title: put them . . . into ward.
entries.content: put them . . . into ward. Second step: to alarm.

entries.title: live.
entries.content: live. Figure of speech Heterosis (of Mood). Hebrew "this do and ye shall live".

entries.title: guilty.
entries.content:
guilty. The treatment begins to take effect.

his soul. Hebrew. nephesh ( App-13 ). His anguish emphasized.

entries.title: Reuben.
entries.content:
Reuben. See Genesis 37:21 .

Spake. Compare Genesis 37:21 . Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 .

entries.title: understood.
entries.content:
understood. Hebrew was listening.

he spake, &c. = for the interpreter was between them.

entries.title: Simeon.
entries.content: Simeon. Probably because his cruel nature (Genesis 34:25 , Compare Genesis 49:5 ) made him the deviser of the evil.

entries.title: lo.
entries.content:
lo. Figure of speech. Asterismos. App-6 .

failed them. Hebrew. "went out". Figure of speech Hyperbole ( App-6 ).

entries.title: roughly.
entries.content:
roughly. Compare Genesis 42:7 .

took us for. Or, set us down as.

entries.title: are no spies.
entries.content: are no spies. Hebrew have never proved spies.

entries.title: one is not.
entries.content: one is not. Some codices, with Samaritan Pentateuch and Syriac, read "but the one is not". And this is all they have to say of Genesis 37:28 !

entries.title: food.
entries.content: food. Aram, and Septuagint read "corn".

entries.title: so will I, &c.
entries.content: so will I, &c. Some codices, with Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate, read "and your brother will I deliver up to you".

entries.title: of my children.
entries.content: of my children. No Ellipsis. These italics unnecessary.

entries.title: then,
entries.content:
then, &c. Figure of speech Euphemismos ( App-6 ), for "then shall ye kill me".

bring down. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Effect), i.e. ye will be the cause of it.

my gray hairs. Figure of speech Metonymy (of the Adjunct). i.e. "me in my old age".

the grave. Hebrew. Sheol. See note on Genesis 37:35 and App-35 .

entries.title: did solemnly protest.
entries.content: did solemnly protest. Hebrew "protesting he protested". Figure of speech Polyptoton ( App-6 ). See note on Genesis 26:28 .

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content:
Israel. Note the name. Jacob is used of his weakness (Genesis 42:36 , &c), Israel of his resignation to God's will. In this use of the names Jacob and Israel, men might well invent a Jacobite and Israelite authorship, as well as an Elohist and Jehovist theory!

ill. Hebrew. R a'a. See App-44 .

entries.title: asked us straitly.
entries.content:
asked us straitly. Hebrew "asking he asked us". Figure of speech Polyptoton . See note on Genesis 43:3 above, and Genesis 26:28 .

could we certainly know. Hebrew "knowing could we know". Figure of speech Polyptoton . See note on Genesis 26:28 ,

entries.title: forever.
entries.content: forever. Hebrew "all the days".

entries.title: best fruits in the land.
entries.content: best fruits in the land. Hebrew "the praise of the land". Figure of speech Metonymy (of the Cause). App-6 . "Praise" put for the choice fruits which called forth the praise.

entries.title: God Almighty.
entries.content:
God Almighty. Hebrew. El Shaddai. App-4 .

mercy. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause). Mercy put for the favours shown.

entries.title: house.
entries.content:
house. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). House put for the servants of it.

slay. Hebrew "slay a slaying". Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 , = slay abundantly.

entries.title: as
entries.content: as = according as.

entries.title: we came indeed.
entries.content: we came indeed. Hebrew "coming down, we came down". Figure of speech Polyptoton. See note on Genesis 26:28

entries.title: Peace.
entries.content:
Peace. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species). Peace put for all its blessings.

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

treasure = hidden or secret treasure.

entries.title: bread.
entries.content: bread. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species). App-6 . Bread put for all kinds of food.

entries.title: bowed themselves.
entries.content: bowed themselves. Some codices, with Septuagint and Vulg, add "with their faces". Compare Genesis 37:7 , Genesis 37:8 .

entries.title: your father . . . the old man
entries.content: your father . . . the old man = your aged father.

entries.title: bowed down, &c.
entries.content: bowed down, &c. Compare Genesis 37:7-10 .

entries.title: Benjamin.
entries.content: Benjamin. Now twenty-two, and father of ten sons. Compare Genesis 46:21 .

entries.title: wept.
entries.content: wept. See note on Genesis 42:24 .

entries.title: they sat.
entries.content:
they sat. Egyptian pictures show that it was the custom to sit at meals.

firstborn. Joseph thus showing that he knew their ages and order, and causing them to marvel.

youngest, &c. This was to try them, and see whether they were still "moved with envy". Compare Genesis 37:4 , Genesis 37:8 , Genesis 37:11 , Genesis 37:18 . It was also a type of the coming day, when the true Joseph will be able to do for the scattered and mingled tribes what was done here for the tribal heads. Compare Zechariah 12:9-14 .

marvelled [and looked] at one another. Figure of speech Ellipsis ( App-6 ), thus supplied.

entries.title: took and sent, &c.
entries.content:
took and sent, &c. Hebrew "lifted liftings". Figure of speech Polyptoton , for emphasis = sent choice portions.

five times. The number of grace. See App-10 , and Compare Genesis 41:34 ; Genesis 45:22 ; Genesis 47:2 , Genesis 47:24 .

were merry. Hebrew drank abundantly. Compare Haggai 1:6 . John 2:10 .

entries.title: men.
entries.content: men. Hebrew, plural of ish , or 'enosh. App-14 .

entries.title: cup.
entries.content:
cup. Hebrew. gebi'a, out of which wine was poured: distinguishing from the smaller cups from which it was drunk. Jeremiah 35:5 .

youngest. This was the fourth step to try them, and to prove whether they were the same brethren still, and would treat Benjamin as they had treated Joseph.

entries.title: Wherefore.
entries.content: Wherefore. Figure of speech Erotesis. App-6 . Septuagint and Syriac insert "Wherefore then have ye the silver cup? "

entries.title: divineth.
entries.content:
divineth. This was to confirm their belief that Joseph was an Egyptian. Emphasized by Figure of speech Polyptoton . Hebrew divining he divineth.

evil. Hebrew. R'a'a. See App-44 .

entries.title: God forbid.
entries.content: God forbid. No word for "God" here. Hebrew = Far be it from thy servants.

entries.title: let him die.
entries.content: let him die. This was the penalty in the Code of Khammurabi, with which they were acquainted in Canaan (6); death for stealing from a palace. Property more sacred than life.

entries.title: What . . . ?
entries.content:
What . . . ? Figure of speech Erotesis ( App-6 ).

God hath found out. This confession was what Joseph had been labouring to procure. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

iniquity. Hebrew. 'avon. See App-44 .

entries.title: Judah.
entries.content: Judah. He who proposed to sell Joseph and save his life (Genesis 37:26 , Genesis 37:27 ), now proposes to remain a bondman for Benjamin. He had already become surety for his Safety (Genesis 43:8 , Genesis 43:9 ).

entries.title: I said.
entries.content: I said. Here Joseph learned what happened after they had sold him; and how they had deceived their father (Genesis 37:31 , Genesis 37:32 ).

entries.title: my gray hairs.
entries.content:
my gray hairs. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct). App-6 . = "me, in my old age".

the grave. Hebrew. Sheol. See note on Genesis 37:35 , and App-35 . The whole phrase is a Euphemism ( App-6 ) for "ye will kill me"; so Genesis 44:31 , "he will die".

entries.title: life
entries.content: life = soul. Hebrew. nephesh. See App-13 .

entries.title: with us.
entries.content: with us. Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Syriac have the words in the text.

entries.title: see.
entries.content:
see. Put by Metonymy (of Cause) for the feelings produced by seeing them. Note the Ellipsis "see [and grieve over] the evil, "&c.

come. Hebrew find. Evil is thus personified, by Figure of speech Prosopopoeia.

entries.title: wept aloud.
entries.content: wept aloud. Hebrew gave [forth] his voice in weeping, showing the intensity of feeling. See note on Genesis 42:24 .

entries.title: I am Joseph.
entries.content:
I am Joseph. So the true Joseph will one day reveal Himself, and His brethren will then be troubled indeed. Revelation 1:7 . Matthew 24:30 . Zechariah 12:9-14 .

doth, &c. Figure of speech Erotesis ( App-6 ). For he had just been informed of the fact (Genesis 43:28 ).

entries.title: whom ye sold.
entries.content: whom ye sold. Words adopted by Stephen (Acts 7:9 ).

entries.title: be not grieved, &c.
entries.content:
be not grieved, &c. Compare Acts 3:17 .

nor angry, &c. Hebrew "let not anger kindle in your eyes". Figure of speech Prosopopoeia.

God did send. So, Genesis 45:7 ; Genesis 50:20 . Psalms 105:17 . Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

preserve life. i.e. to preserve you a posterity in the earth (Genesis 45:7 ), and hence, to ensure the birth of the true Joseph, and all who have life eternal in Him.

entries.title: earing
entries.content: earing = ploughing (Anglo-Saxon).

entries.title: God.
entries.content:
God. Hebrew. ha Elohim (with definite article) for emphasis = the Triune God Himself.

made me. The Severus Codex reads "lent me". See App-34 .

a father to Pharaoh. This is not the Hebrew Ab , "father"; but Ab en Perao is an Egyptian title of high office of state. See on Genesis 41:43 = first minister of Pharaoh's household.

entries.title: children
entries.content: children = sons. And so throughout.

entries.title: that.
entries.content: that. Hebrew because, showing the Ellipsis (i.e. Brachyology) ; read "Benjamin; because my own mouth is speaking unto you [I cannot speak of all my glory], but ye shall tell my father of all my glory".

entries.title: Now thou art commanded.
entries.content:
Now thou art commanded. Septuagint and Vulgate read "Thou, therefore, command them".

wagons. Not yet used in Canaan. Those in Egypt depicted as having two wheels.

entries.title: regard not your stuff.
entries.content: regard not your stuff. Hebrew let not your eye pity. Figure of speech Prosopopoeia.

entries.title: commandment.
entries.content: commandment. Hebrew mouth, put by Metonymy (of Cause), App-6 , for command given by it.

entries.title: he gave.
entries.content: he gave. Compare Genesis 43:34 .

entries.title: Jacob's.
entries.content:
Jacob's. Hebrew his. Compare Genesis 45:28 .

fainted = began to cease beating. Compare Jacob's fainting, with Israel's "strength", Genesis 45:28 . Genesis 45:27 spirit. Hebrew. ruach, put by Metonymy (OF Cause), lor its manifestations. See App-9 .

Jacob. Note this name connected with unbelief (Genesis 45:20 ) and weakness, and

entries.title: Israel,
entries.content: Israel, which is used in connection with his strength of faith, and Act 46:1 . Compare Israel's strength, with Jacob's fainting, Genesis 45:26 .

entries.title: offered sacrifices.
entries.content: offered sacrifices. Hebrew. zabach. App-43 .

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content:
Israel. See note on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

Jacob, Jacob. Figure of speech Epizeuxis, App-6 , for emphasis. To remind him of what he was and had been, in contrast to what God would make him.

entries.title: fear not, &c.
entries.content: fear not, &c. Though Isaac forbidden to go (Genesis 26:2 ), and Abraham warned (Genesis 15:13 , Genesis 15:14 ), no need to fear where God goes with Jacob and us.

entries.title: surely bring thee up.
entries.content:
surely bring thee up. Figure of speech Polyptoton. Compare Genesis 15:14 .

put his hand, &c. i.e. shall close thine eyes in peace.

entries.title: sons of Israel carried Jacob.
entries.content:
sons of Israel carried Jacob. They now take the ground of faith.

wagons. See note on Genesis 45:19 .

entries.title: daughters.
entries.content: daughters. Compare Genesis 31:55 with Genesis 46:15 , Genesis 46:17 .

entries.title: the names.
entries.content: the names. Compare the above order with that of Genesis 49:3-27 , and see App-45 .

entries.title: Merari.
entries.content: Merari. Jochebed is to be added, for she "came into" Egypt in her mother (Numbers 26:59 ).

entries.title: but Er and Onan.
entries.content:
but Er and Onan. These are not to be reckoned.

Hezron and Hamul. These grandsons take their place.

entries.title: souls of his sons.
entries.content: souls of his sons. Hebrew. nephesh. Souls put by Synecdoche (of the Part) for the persons ( App-6 ). And "of" = the Genitive of Apposition: i.e. "the souls, that is to say, his sons, "&c. ( App-17 ).

entries.title: were born.
entries.content: were born. Some codices, with Samaritan Pentateuch, Targum of Onkelos, Septuagint, and Syriac, read "whom she bare".

entries.title: sons.
entries.content: sons. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species). Only one mentioned; some codices read "son".

entries.title: out of his loins.
entries.content:
out of his loins. This is said in order to distinguish the numbers sixtysix and seventy from Stephen's seventy-five, in Acts 7:14 , which includes Jacob as well as "all his kindred " (which are not included in the direct descendants of this verse). These extra nine are made up in part by the five in 1 Chronicles 7:14-20 (Machir, Gilead, Shuthelah, Tahath, Eden, as in Septuagint: also here).

threescore and six. See note on Genesis 46:8 .

entries.title: threescore and ten.
entries.content: threescore and ten. 7 x 10. See App-10 . These seventy (Exodus 1:5 .Ruth 4:11; Ruth 4:11 ) are in contrast with the seventy nations of Genesis 10 , and in correspondence with the seventy elders (Exodus 24:1 .Numbers 11:16; Numbers 11:16 ).

entries.title: Judah.
entries.content:
Judah. See Genesis 44:18 and Compare Genesis 37:26 .

Goshen. The land east of Memphis, suitable for grazing, called "the field of Zoan". Zoan (or Tanis) mentioned in the Inscriptions as containing non- Egyptian inhabitants and Semites.

entries.title: shepherds.
entries.content: shepherds. See on Genesis 46:34 .

entries.title: abomination.
entries.content: abomination. Metonymy (of Adjunct). = an abominable person. Apepi, the Pharaoh of Joseph, was one of the Hyksos, or shepherd kings. Joseph's advice would commend his brethren to Pharaoh (Genesis 47:6 ), and keep them separate from the Egyptians, It was a race prejudice, not a class prejudice.

entries.title: Goshen.
entries.content: Goshen. See on Genesis 46:28 .

entries.title: his brethren.
entries.content: his brethren. Samaritan Pentateuch, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, Syriac read "the brethren of Joseph". five. The number of grace. See App-10 .

entries.title: Jacob.
entries.content: Jacob. See notes on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

entries.title: How old . . . ?
entries.content: How old . . . ? Hebrew How many are the days? The first question asked in the East to-day.

entries.title: days.
entries.content:
days. Joined with years = Figure of speech Pleonasm. App-6 .

pilgrimage = sojournings.

an hundred and thirty years. Joseph being 39; Reuben 46; Simeon 45; Levi 44 Judah 43. Two hundred and fifteen years from Abrarn's call from Clialdea.

entries.title: Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
entries.content: Jacob blessed Pharaoh. "The less is blessed of the better" (Hebrews 7:7 ). Compare Genesis 47:2 .

entries.title: Rameses.
entries.content:
Rameses. Later name of Goshen. See Exodus 1:11 .

as = according as.

entries.title: gathered up:
entries.content: gathered up: i. e. caused it to be gathered up. Figure of speech. Metonymy (of Cause). App-6 .

entries.title: gathered up:
entries.content: gathered up: i.e. caused it to be gathered up. Figure of speech Metonymy .

entries.title: all the Egyptians.
entries.content:
all the Egyptians. Hebrew all Egypt. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject). App-6 .

why should we die? Figure of speech Erotesis.

entries.title: you.
entries.content: you. Samaritan Pentateuch, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, and Septuagint add "bread".

entries.title: our land.
entries.content:
our land. Figure of speech. Prosopopmia. App-6 .

live, and not die. Figure of speech Pleonasm.

entries.title: removed them to cities.
entries.content: removed them to cities. Samaritan Pentateuch, Pentateuch, and Vulgate read, "made them serve as servants " ; or, made them bondmen".

entries.title: removed them to cities.
entries.content: removed them to cities. Samaritan Pentateuch, Pentateuch, and Vulgate read, "made them serve as servants"; or, "made them bondmen".

entries.title: portion.
entries.content:
portion. Hebrew "statute". Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Genus). Statute is put for the portion allowed by it.

sold not. The reference of Herodotus to this is thus proved to be correct.

entries.title: Behold . . . lo.
entries.content: Behold . . . lo. Figure of speech. Asterismos. App-6 .

entries.title: fifth part.
entries.content: fifth part. This is the Turkish law in Palestine to-day, if the landlord supplies cattle and seed. So the terms would not be too onerous.

entries.title: a law.
entries.content: a law. Hebrew. chok, decree.

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content: Israel. Used here, for the first time, of the nation. grew, and multiplied, &c. Fulfilling Genesis 46:3 , and preparing for Exodus 1:7 with Exodus 12:37 .

entries.title: the whole age.
entries.content: the whole age. Hebrew the days of the years of his life. Figure of speech Pleonasm. This charge concerning his burial to be distinguished from the charge to all his sons.

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content: Israel. Used here of the man Jacob. See notes on Genesis 47:27 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

entries.title: as
entries.content: as = according as.

entries.title: Israel bowed himself.
entries.content: Israel bowed himself. Much confusion caused by supposing Hebrews 11:21 refers to this. Mistake made by Ancient Versions and modern commentators. Hebrews 11:21 refers to his blessing of Joseph's sons. This refers to the charge concerning his burial. It may or may not be bed, or staff.

entries.title: after these things.
entries.content: after these things. The blessing of Joseph's sons took place after Jacob's charge concerning his burial.

entries.title: Jacob . . . Israel.
entries.content: Jacob . . . Israel. See note on use of these names, Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 . sat upon the bed. This is neither leaning on it nor worshipping. Compare Genesis 48:12 .

entries.title: GOD ALMIGHTY.
entries.content:
GOD ALMIGHTY. Hebrew. 'El Shaddai. See App-4 .

Luz. Compare Genesis 28:13 , Genesis 28:19 ; Genesis 35:6 .

entries.title: and.
entries.content: and. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton, to emphasise the four parts of the blessing.

entries.title: are.
entries.content: are. Hebrew they [are] mine. The united preference of Joseph's two sons.

entries.title: Rachel died.
entries.content: Rachel died. Compare Genesis 35:19 .

entries.title: God.
entries.content: God. Hebrew. Elohim. with art. = God Himself.

entries.title: he bowed himself,
entries.content: he bowed himself, i.e. Jacob worshipped; and, as we know from the Divine addition in Hebrews 11:21 , he leaned on his staff = sitting on the (Egyptian) bed (Genesis 48:2 ).

entries.title: guiding his hands wittingly
entries.content: guiding his hands wittingly (i.e. knowingly), Figure of speech Prosopopoeia. Hebrew "making his hands to understand".

entries.title: walk
entries.content: walk = walk habitually (Hebrew. Hithpael) .

entries.title: Note
entries.content:
Note the three titles in verses: Genesis 48:15 , Genesis 48:16 .

The Angel = the creature form of the second person as the messenger of Jehovah (Elohim as consecrated by oath). This form not assumed for the occasion, but for permanent communion with His creatures (Genesis 3:8 ; Genesis 15:1 ; Genesis 17:1 ; Genesis 18:1 , Genesis 18:2 ; Genesis 28:13 ; Genesis 32:24 , Genesis 32:30 . Exodus 23:20 , Exodus 23:21 .Numbers 22:21 .Joshua 5:13-15 .Proverbs 8:22-31 .Malachi 3:1; 1 Chronicles 1:15 .Revelation 3:14; Revelation 3:14 ).

redeemed. Hebrew. g'aal = to redeem (by payment of charge).

See note on Exodus 6:6 .

grow = swarm as fishes. earth, or the land.

entries.title: displeased.
entries.content: displeased. Hebrew was evil in his eyes.

entries.title: Not so, &c.
entries.content: Not so, &c. This was Joseph's "will", which Jacob's faith overcame.

entries.title: refused.
entries.content:
refused. This is Jacob's faith overcoming "the will of man" (Hebrews 11:20 , as Isaac's faith overcame "the will of the flesh", Genesis 27 . Hebrews 11:20 .

greater. Fulfilled. Compare Numbers 1:32-35 ; Numbers 2:18-20 . Deuteronomy 33:17 .

multitude = assembly, or convocation. Hebrew. kohal, to call, or muster.

entries.title: portion.
entries.content:
portion. Hebrew. Shechem, Greek. Sychar, see John 4:5 . Both Abraham and Jacob bought property at Shechem. Genesis 23:18 , Genesis 23:19 ; Genesis 33:18 , Genesis 33:19 ; and here supplemental history tells how Jacob recovered it out of the hand of the Amorite who must have seized it. Figure of speech Hysteresis. App-6 .

above: i.e. the double portion of the firstborn, which Reuben forfeited. Compare Deuteronomy 21:17 . Compare 1 Chronicles 5:2 .Ezekiel 47:13 .

entries.title: Jacob.
entries.content:
Jacob. See notes on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 . which shall befall you. This blessing (Genesis 49:28 ) is therefore direct prophecy.

the last days. First occurance of fourteen: Genesis 49:1 .Numbers 24:14 .Deuteronomy 4:30 ; Deuteronomy 31:29 . Isaiah 2:2 .Jeremiah 23:20 ; Jeremiah 30:24 ; Jeremiah 48:47 ; Jeremiah 49:39 . Ezekiel 38:16 . Daniel 2:28 ; Daniel 10:14 .Hosea 3:5 .Micah 4:1 . In ten of these rendered "latter days". A study of these will show that the prophecy (Genesis 49:1 ) and "blessing" (Genesis 49:28 ) extends to, and embraces the days of Messiah, and His first and second advents.

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content: Israel. See notes on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

entries.title: Reuben.
entries.content: Reuben. See Genesis 49:28 , Compare Genesis 46:8-25 , and App-45 .

entries.title: Unstable as water.
entries.content:
Unstable as water. Figure of speech Simile. Compare Numbers 16:1 , Numbers 16:2 ; Numbers 32:1 .

water . . . thou. Figure of speech Ellipsis here ( App-6 . b). The word "unstable" = to flow down, and requires the Ellipsis to be filled up thus: "Flowing down as water [passes away, so] thou shalt not excel". What thus would pass away is set forth in Genesis 49:3 , and so it came to pass (1 Chronicles 5:1 ).

entries.title: my soul
entries.content:
my soul = myself. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

secret = council.

unto. Samaritan Pentateuch, The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel, Septuagint, and Syriac insert "and" = "and into".

assembly. Hebrew. kahal = Greek. eeclesia. See Genesis 28:3 .

digged down a wall. Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint read "hamstrung an ox". Compare Genesis 34:26 .

entries.title: divide.
entries.content:
divide. Fulfilled, Joshua 19:1 . 1 Chronicles 4:39-43 .Leviticus 25:32-34 . Levi's turned to blessing later, Exodus 32:26-29 . Deuteronomy 10:8 , Deuteronomy 10:9 .

Jacob. First occurance as used of the whole nation.

Israel. See note on Genesis 34:7 . Compare Genesis 47:27 .

entries.title: Judah
entries.content:
Judah = Praise. Figure of speech Paronomasia ( App-6 ). " Jehuda, Joducha ".

bow down. Compare 2 Samuel 5:1-8 and Psalms 72:11 .Philippians 1:2 , Philippians 1:10 .

entries.title: is.
entries.content:
is. Figure of speech Metaphor. Rest of verse is Allegory. App-6 .

lion. See note on Numbers 2:32 .

entries.title: sceptre.
entries.content:
sceptre. First occ Put by Metonymy (of Adjunct) for Him Who holds it. Septuagint and Targ read "ruler". See Numbers 24:17 . Psalms 45:6 . Zechariah 10:11 .

lawgiver. First occurance. Compare Numbers 21:18 . Deuteronomy 33:21 .Psalms 60:7 ; Psalms 108:8 . Isaiah 33:22 .

from between his feet = from his posterity. Put by Fig, Euphemy ( App-6 ). Septuagint and Targum of Onkelos read "from his thighs", i.e. "his seed". Compare Deuteronomy 28:57 .

until Shiloh come = until He, Shiloh, comes. So Aq., Sym., Syriac. Note the six Pentateuch titles: "Seed" (Genesis 3:15 ), "Shiloh" (Genesis 49:10 ), "Sceptre" (Genesis 49:10 ), "Shepherd" and "Stone" (Genesis 49:24 ), "Star" (Numbers 24:17 ).

gathering. Hebrew. yikhah = obedience, submission (not kabaz, as in Jeremiah 31:10 ). Note the Structure of this verse ( Alternation ). a | The Sceptre shall not depart from Judah, a | Until He, Shiloh, come [Whose right it is, Ez. Genesis 21:27 ] b | Nor a Lawgiver from his seed, b | And [until] to Him, [the Lawgiver, shall be] the obedience of the peoples.

entries.title: vine.
entries.content:
vine. So plentiful in Judah, that people were without care in such matters.

wine. Hebrew. yayin ( App-27 ). There was more than enough to lavish.

entries.title: Issachar.
entries.content: Issachar. Original Orth = he bringeth reward; referring to birth, Genesis 30:18 (compare Psalms 24:5 .Ecclesiastes 5:18 . Esther 2:9 , &c.) But here = a hireling. The prophecy is: "The hireling is the ass (or saddle-bearer) of strangers, Couching down among the folds; When he saw rest that it was good, And the land that it was pleasant:" &c. He preferred to pay tribute to the Canaanites rather than engage in the struggle to expel them.

entries.title: Dan shall judge.
entries.content:
Dan shall judge. Figure of speech Paronomasia. App-6 . Dan Jadin, Compare Genesis 30:6 . Fulfilled in Judges 15:20 .

tribes. Hebrew sceptres (Genesis 49:10 ). Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct). Put for ruler.

entries.title: a serpent.
entries.content:
a serpent. Beguiling to idolatry. The first tribe to do so. See note on Judges 18:30 . Hence omitted in Revelation 7:4 (compare Deuteronomy 29:18-21 .Leviticus 24:10-16 ; 1 Kings 12:30 . 2 Kings 10:29 ).

heels. Compare Genesis 3:15 .Jeremiah 8:16 , Jeremiah 8:17 .

entries.title: salvation.
entries.content:
salvation. Figure of speech Metonymy (of Effect). Put for Him Who brings deliverance from all the works of the old serpent (Isaiah 25:8 , Isaiah 25:9 . Matthew 24:13 ). See App-36 .

LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

entries.title: Gad.
entries.content:
Gad. Hebrew. Gad gedud. Figure of speech Paronomasia. App-6 .

overcome him = "shall troop (or press) upon him, but he shall press upon their heel".

entries.title: Out of
entries.content:
Out of The Hebrew letter "m", which should end Genesis 49:19 , making it "upon their heels", has been wrongly prefixed to the next word, "Asher", Genesis 49:20 , thus making "Asher" begin "Out of", unlike all the others. It should read: "He shall press upon their heels, Asher, his bread shall be, "&c. The Revised Version rightly keeps the Hebrew letter "m" at end of Genesis 49:19 , but repeats it at beginning of Genesis 49:20 , thus translating it twice!

bread. Put for all food. Figure of speech Synecdoche (of Species). App-6 .

entries.title: let loose.
entries.content:
let loose. Emphasis on freedom. he giveth = he it is that giveth.

goodly words = song of Deborah. Judges 5:18 .

entries.title: Joseph.
entries.content:
Joseph. Compare Deuteronomy 33:13-17 .

whose branches run over the wall = branches [it hath] each hath overclimbed a wall.

entries.title: sorely grieved.
entries.content: sorely grieved. Compare Amos 6:6 .

entries.title: God
entries.content: God = One.

entries.title: the.
entries.content: the. Should be 'El = GOD (with Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, and Syriac)

entries.title: separate
entries.content: separate = or set apart. Hebrew. nazir, the consecrated one.

entries.title: ravin, &c.
entries.content: ravin, &c. Compare the Benjamites, Judges 3:15 . 1 Samuel 11:6-11 ; 1 Samuel 14:13-48 . Acts 7:58 ; Acts 8:1 , Acts 8:3 ; Acts 9:13 , Acts 9:14 , Acts 9:21 ; Acts 22:4-8 . 1 Timothy 1:13 .
The sons collectively. See App-45 .

entries.title: gathered unto my people.
entries.content:
gathered unto my people. Figure of speech Euphemy. Put for "death and burial". See Genesis 49:33 . See note on Genesis 49:33 .

with my fathers. Compare Genesis 23:9 , Genesis 23:10 ; Genesis 47:30 .

entries.title: bought.
entries.content: bought. Compare Genesis 23:16 .

entries.title: Abraham.
entries.content: Abraham. The five previously buried there form an acrostic of the sixth. Isaac, Sarah, Rebekah, Abraham, Leah = Israel (Hebrews 11:13 ).

entries.title: yielded up the ghost.
entries.content:
yielded up the ghost. The spirit going to God who gave it (Ecclesiastes 12:7 . Numbers 16:22 ; Numbers 27:16 ).

gathered unto his people. Refers to body, as the previous gathering (Genesis 49:33 ) refers to his feet. See on Genesis 49:29 . He was aged 147.

entries.title: wept.
entries.content: wept. See note on Genesis 42:24 .

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content: Israel. See notes on Genesis 32:28 ; Genesis 43:8 ; Genesis 45:26 , Genesis 45:28 .

entries.title: for so, &c.
entries.content: for so, &c. Israelites never embalmed. Hence the need of this parenthetical explanation.

entries.title: Joseph spake.
entries.content: Joseph spake. He could not speak before, for, in mourning, Egyptians never shaved, and Joseph, therefore, was not presentable. See on Genesis 41:14 .

entries.title: digged.
entries.content: digged. Hence, probably rock-hewn.

entries.title: And.
entries.content: And. Note the Figure of speech Polysyndeton ( App-6 ), emphasizing each party.

entries.title: Atad.
entries.content:
Atad. Probably named after the owner, as 2 Samuel 6:6 , "Nachon's"; 2 Samuel 24:16 , "Araunah's".

Abel-mizraim = the mourning of the Egyptians.

entries.title: his sons . . . buried him.
entries.content:
his sons . . . buried him. See note on Acts 7:16 .

bought. Compare Genesis 23:10 .
The final section of Genesis.

entries.title: Joseph wept.
entries.content: Joseph wept. See note on Genesis 42:24 .

entries.title: fell down.
entries.content:
fell down. Compare Genesis 37:7-10 .

Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos. App-6 .

entries.title: am I, &c.
entries.content: am I, &c. Figure of speech Erotesis . Septuagint reads "I am in the place of God". The Syriac and Arab, read "I fear God".

entries.title: God meant it, &c.
entries.content:
God meant it, &c. Compare Psalms 105:17 . Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

alive. See on Genesis 45:5 .

entries.title: kindly.
entries.content: kindly. Hebrew spake unto their hearts.

entries.title: Machir.
entries.content:
Machir. Compare Numbers 26:29 ; Numbers 32:39 . Joshua 17:1 .

brought up, &c. Hebrew born. See Genesis 30:3 , i.e., were adopted by him as soon as they were born.

entries.title: surely visit you.
entries.content: surely visit you. (Exodus 3:16 .) Figure of speech Polyptoton. Hebrew "visiting will visit you"; used for great emphasis. See note on Genesis 26:28 . This was the faith of Joseph referred to in Hebrews 11:22 . He had "heard" (Romans 10:17 ) and believed what God had said to Abraham. Genesis 12:7 ; Genesis 15:18 ; Genesis 13:14 , Genesis 13:15 ; Isaiah 26:3 , Isaiah 26:4 ; Jam 28:13 ; Jam 35:12 ; Jam 48:1-4 . All three names are united and discriminated in Exodus 2:24 ; Exodus 3:6 . Psalms 105:9 , Psalms 105:10 . And compare Exodus 6:3 , Exodus 6:4 .Deuteronomy 11:21 .Luke 1:72 , Luke 1:73 , &c.

entries.title: carry up my bones from hence.
entries.content:
carry up my bones from hence. Which they did. See Exodus 13:19 . Joshua 24:32 . So Jacob had charged them. Genesis 49:29 , Genesis 49:30 , and so they had done, Genesis 50:7-13 .

hence. Some codices, with Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint, Syriac, and one printed edition (1494), add "with you".

entries.title: a coffin.
entries.content: a coffin. Thus the book of Genesis begins with God, and ends with man. It begins with the creation of the heavens above, and ends with "a coffin in Egypt".
